title: Engineering Operations Technician, AWS Infrastructure Services
descriptionHtml:
Join our dynamic team and become a critical guardian of technological infrastructure! As a Data Center Engineering Technician, you'll play a pivotal role in maintaining the heartbeat of mission-critical technology infrastructure, ensuring seamless operations that power global digital experiences. Your expertise will directly contribute to maintaining an extraordinary 99.999% uptime, keeping the digital world running smoothly and efficiently.

Engineering Technicians are Amazon’s front line when it comes to hands-on electrical and mechanical equipment troubleshooting. They will maintain, operate, and troubleshoot, Data Center Operation’s Mission Critical Facilities, which includes stand-by diesel generators and related fuel systems, as well as three phase electrical systems such as: switch gear, UPSs, PDUs, wet cell batteries and associated systems, CRAC, centrifugal chillers, cooling towers/water chemical system, air handlers and associated systems, pumps, & motors.

AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

NOTE: Amazon does not sponsor for immigration, including for H-1B, TN, and other non-immigrant visas, for this role.

NOTE: Lump sum stipend will be provided to eligible candidates who relocate for this position.

Key job responsibilities
- Daily building rounds to monitor and record information from electrical, mechanical, and fire/life safety equipment to ensure 24/7 reliability and availability

- Monitor Building Management Systems (BMS) and Electrical Power Management System (EPMS)

- Assist in troubleshooting of facility and rack-level events within internal Service Level Agreements (SLA)

- Perform rack installs and rack decommissioning within internal SLA

- Perform PM, troubleshooting, root cause analysis, and repair of electrical and mechanical equipment

- Technical writing to support change management program

- Monitor daily work requests and manage to resolution, and execute projects from conception to completion

- On-site support of contractors, sub-contractors and vendors, ensuring that all work performed is in accordance with established practices, procedures & local legislation

- Work schedule changes depending on specific site needs. Shifts can be up to 12 hours and may rotate on a predefined schedule. Some locations have on-call rotations.

- Role may support more than one location/site.

Physical Requirements:

- Willingness and demonstrated ability to work in the following physical conditions with reasonable accommodations:

- Regularly lift and/or move up to 39 pounds independently

- Participate in group lifts for 40+ pounds

- Maintain balance and perform construction tasks while on a ladder

- Regularly walk, use hands and fingers, handle or feel, reach with hands and arms, stoop, kneel, crouch or crawl, climb stairs, twist, bend, work above shoulders, grasp, carry, push and pull objects into position

- Work in an environment requiring provided ear protection

- This role supports data centers in various operational stages. The position may be assigned to a facility still under development, which could require travel to established locations for training until your designated site becomes fully operational.

Essential Requirements:

- Ability to travel to or commute between data center locations as needed

- Willingness to temporarily work at alternative sites during training periods or until assigned facility is operational

- Travel frequency will vary based on business needs and operational status of assigned facility

- Candidates must be able to travel (over 50 miles) or commute (less than 50 miles) to active data center sites as required by business needs.

A day in the life
This role acts as Amazon’s front line when it comes to hands-on electrical and mechanical equipment preventative maintenance (PM) and troubleshooting, reporting to a site’s Data Center Facility Manager (FM). They will maintain, operate, and troubleshoot mission-critical data center facility equipment including stand-by diesel generators and related fuel systems, 3 phase electrical systems such as switchgear, UPS units, PDUs, and wet cell batteries and associated systems. Mechanical equipment includes CRAHU units, centrifugal chillers, cooling towers, water systems, air handlers and associated systems, pumps, and motors. Additional support equipment is included in the scope of the role which includes fire/life safety equipment, building automation systems, and general facilities equipment.

- 2+ years of electrical facilities maintenance and 1+ years of mechanical facilities maintenance experience
- 2+ years of Microsoft Office products and applications experience

Preferred qualifications

- 2+ years of data center engineering experience
- Experience reading and writing procedures, technical documents, and engineering drawings

title: Sr. System Development Engineer, Antenna System Validation
descriptionHtml:
Amazon Leo is a long-term Amazon program to increase global broadband access through a constellation of satellites in Low Earth Orbit (LEO); providing low-latency, high-speed broadband connectivity to unserved and underserved communities around the world. Direct-to-Device (D2D) is Leo's initiative to enable standard smartphones and IoT devices to connect directly to satellites, filling coverage gaps in remote areas.

As a System Development Engineer, you will design and develop hardware, firmware, and/or software solutions for antenna systems supporting both our current production satellites and new programs including D2D and our next-generation satellite constellation. You'll work closely with hardware, RF, and software teams to bring up, test, and ship systems that combine custom hardware, FPGAs, and embedded firmware and see your work in the lab or in orbit.

Export Control Requirement:
Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

Key job responsibilities
- Own design and implementation of hardware, firmware, software, or FPGA components for antenna systems
- Collaborate with systems architects and cross-functional hardware, firmware, and software teams to define, implement, test, and release new antenna hardware and software capabilities
- Support bring-up, characterization, and validation of antenna subsystems in the lab and on test hardware
- Troubleshoot and resolve hardware, firmware, and software issues found during development, integration, or production testing
- Contribute to design reviews and technical documentation for new hardware, firmware, and software

A day in the life
Most days, you're working with cross-functional teams talking through requirements with antenna and hardware engineers, sketching out designs, and writing documentation others will rely on. Some days you're in the lab instead, hands on the hardware.

About the team
Our team validates payload phased arrays. The antennas we work with are packed with many processors and hundreds/thousands of individual elements working in sync. We test designs, find what breaks, and build the tools that make that possible. We partner closely with antenna, hardware, and firmware engineers. We take pride in catching problems before launch since once it's in orbit, there's no fixing it by hand.

Basic qualifications

- 5+ years of programming with at least one modern language such as C++, C#, Java, Python, Golang, PowerShell, Ruby experience
- Bachelor's degree in computer science, electrical engineering, or related field
- Experience with digital design, verification, or embedded firmware development (e.g., SystemVerilog/VHDL RTL, UVM testbenches, or microcontroller firmware)
- Experience using common electronics test equipment (oscilloscopes, power supplies, function generators, etc.)

Preferred qualifications

- Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related technical field
- Experience with FPGA design and implementation using SystemVerilog or VHDL
- Experience with DSP or multi-rate signal processing design
- Experience with phased array antennas or other complex RF systems
- Experience with test automation using Python and lab instrument control (e.g., PyVISA)

title: Sr. Pre-Construction Manager, North America Quick Commerce
descriptionHtml:
Amazon's Quick Commerce team is revolutionizing the customer experience through sub-30-minute delivery by rapidly scaling a first-of-its-kind micro-fulfillment network across North America. We are seeking a highly motivated Sr. Pre-Construction Manager to serve as a senior individual contributor responsible for leading pre-construction strategy and execution across a portfolio of complex retail and logistics projects.

This role is ideal for a strategic builder who thrives in fast-paced, ambiguous environments and can influence cross-functional stakeholders to deliver scalable solutions. The Sr. Pre-Construction Manager will own site due diligence, design development, budgeting, permitting strategy, procurement coordination, and pre-construction execution while partnering closely with Real Estate, Design, Construction, Launch, Operations, Legal, and external consultants. This individual will play a critical role in enabling accelerated delivery timelines while maintaining high standards for cost, quality, and operational readiness.

Successful candidates bring deep experience in construction management, architecture, engineering, development, or owner-side project delivery. The ideal candidate combines strong technical expertise, operational rigor, executive communication skills, and the ability to influence without direct authority while driving complex initiatives across a broad stakeholder network.

Key job responsibilities
- Own pre-construction strategy and execution across a portfolio of Quick Commerce tenant improvement and conversion projects, ensuring alignment on scope, schedule, budget, and launch milestones.
- Lead site due diligence activities, including entitlement review, utility coordination, zoning analysis, permitting strategy, MEP feasibility, and landlord coordination.
- Drive cross-functional alignment with Real Estate, Design, Construction, Launch, Operations, Finance, and Legal to enable successful project delivery.
- Develop and implement standardized processes, scalable mechanisms, and reporting tools that improve portfolio execution and support network expansion.
- Lead RFP development, bid leveling, contractor and consultant procurement, and pre-construction budgeting activities.
- Review conceptual and detailed designs to optimize operational functionality, constructability, schedule, and cost.
- Identify, assess, and resolve permitting, jurisdictional, landlord, utility, and design risks throughout the pre-construction lifecycle.
- Present project status, budgets, schedules, risks, and recommendations to senior leadership and executive stakeholders.
- Drive continuous improvement initiatives focused on reducing costs, shortening project timelines, increasing launch readiness, and improving program standardization.
- Partner with Construction and Launch teams to ensure seamless transitions from pre-construction through project execution and operational handoff.
- Serve as a subject matter expert, providing technical guidance and influencing strategic decisions across the broader Quick Commerce development portfolio.

About the team
Amazon's Quick Commerce team manages projects from site selection through operational handoff, enabling one of Amazon's fastest-growing and most innovative delivery networks through efficient, scalable, and high-quality project delivery. The Pre-Construction organization plays a critical role in accelerating launches by driving alignment across Real Estate, Design, Permitting, Procurement, Construction, and Operations teams. This role offers the opportunity to lead complex, high-impact pre-construction initiatives, influence cross-functional strategy, and help define the future of rapid delivery infrastructure at massive scale through technical expertise, operational excellence, and end-to-end program ownership.

Basic qualifications

- Experience in project or program management
- Bachelor's degree in Construction Management, Architecture, Structural, Civil, Mechanical or Electrical Engineering
- 5+ years of relevant professional experience
- Experience managing and coordinating multiple projects simultaneously

Preferred qualifications

- Experience that includes strong analytical skills, attention to detail, and effective communication abilities
- Master's degree in Construction Management, Architecture, Structural, Civil, Mechanical or Electrical Engineering
- Strong Design, Engineering, or Construction Management experience in the commercial, or industrial warehouse industry.

title: Cluster Manager, PXT Excellence, ROW PXT Japan
descriptionHtml:
Amazon Japan Operations' HR division (PXTX: People Experience and Technology Excellence) is seeking a Cluster PXT Manager.
This role is for someone who is passionate about "achieving significant results with a lean, elite team," who does not cling to conventional approaches, and who can independently build and drive a new HR model that balances standardization and innovation. We are looking for a candidate who thrives in uncertain and changing environments and can demonstrate leadership by autonomously engaging stakeholders.

This is a position where you can build and drive an unprecedented new model within Amazon's HR organization with your own hands. You will gain experience leading large-scale organizational transformation through people management, supporting business operations across more than 100 sites nationwide. As a core member of an innovative initiative that is attracting attention from Amazon's Global HR organization, this is an opportunity to significantly accelerate your career in the HR field. You can leverage your broad HR practical experience while honing your management skills, with a career path toward becoming a regional or divisional HR leader in the future.

At Amazon, you'll work alongside the latest AI and GenAI tools that are increasingly woven into how teams operate: from AI-powered capabilities that accelerate decision-making, to Generative AI that helps you focus on work that truly matters. You'll have opportunities and resources to develop AI fluency at your own pace, with continuous learning built into the culture.

Key job responsibilities
People Management & Talent Development

- People management of PXTX members (HR members based at multiple sites across Japan)
- Development and career growth support for team members (building a successor pipeline)
- Coaching members on their HR work to improve quality of execution in areas such as labor management, organizational development, talent management, recruiting, and employee relations (ER)

Driving and Standardizing HR Generalist Functions
- As a people manager, personally lead complex HR Generalist work (labor management, organizational development, talent management, etc.) and serve as a role model for the team
- Understand the complexities unique to fulfillment and delivery station sites (multi-site operations, shift-based work schedules, management of large-scale hourly workforce, seasonal fluctuation response, etc.) and build/operate standardized processes with a focus on employee experience
- Exercise appropriate judgment and escalation on complex labor and ER cases, and provide guidance and development to team members

Business Partnership & Stakeholder Management
- Build trust-based relationships and maintain/strengthen partnerships with site managers across multiple business units
- Drive cross-functional work and standardization through collaboration with multiple HR teams
- Negotiate and coordinate optimal allocation of business needs and HR resources
- Manage stakeholder expectations and build consensus on priorities

Operational Excellence & Process Improvement
- Lead projects for operational process efficiency and automation
- Team workload management, quality audits, data-driven issue identification and improvement proposals
- Participation in and reporting at business reviews

About the team
PXTX was established in June 2024 as an organization that delivers best-in-class HR partnership to employees through standardized operations and innovative solutions. title: Sr. Software Development Engineer, MONA
descriptionHtml:
AWS runs one of the largest networks in the world, and MONA (Management, Out-of-Band Networks, and Automation) alone owns over one million physical devices across its full lifecycle. We are in the critical path for every new data center powering the AI revolution.

We build the in-house software that solves our hardest network business problems — controllers, software-defined networking (SDN), and planning systems. For example, we own a controller for agentic network auto-remediation, and the planning software that plans every new data center down to capacity and ports. We are looking for a Senior Software Development Engineer to be a technical leader and force multiplier: you will partner with the engineering manager to shape our software strategy while continuing to design and build these systems at fleet scale. If you want the scope to influence what we build and how we build it — and to keep building it yourself — this is that role.


Key job responsibilities
- Partner with the engineering manager to shape the team's software strategy — architecture, roadmap, and long-term vision — for the in-house systems behind a 1M+ device network (everything we run, we build ourselves).
- Design and build the in-house systems that solve our business problems — controllers, software-defined networking (SDN), and planning software — end-to-end, architected to scale with robust tests and metrics.
- Own and evolve our controller for agentic network auto-remediation that detects and resolves network issues automatically.
- Build the planning software that plans every new data center — capacity, racks, and ports — and deploys new network fabric.
- Own out-of-band management-plane services: serial console access to every server and router, plus managed connectivity such as SSH.
- Drive correctness and safety for automation acting on production networks: idempotency, guardrails, and observability that proves work actually happened.
- Lead design reviews, raise the operational-excellence and code-quality bar, and mentor engineers.
- Participate in on-call and help lead high-severity incident response.


A day in the life
No two days look the same. One morning you are whiteboarding with the manager and a principal engineer on how to evolve the control plane for the next wave of AI data centers; the next you are deep in a greenfield auto-remediation service that resolves faults automatically instead of paging a human at 3am. You will make a teammate's design better, unblock a data-center build with capacity planning, and harden out-of-band console access to a million devices. You will see your work land at a scale almost nowhere else can offer — with real autonomy and teammates sharp enough to make you better.

About the team
MONA (Management, Out-of-Band Networks, and Automation) is part of AWS Core Networking. We are a highly motivated team of software, systems, and network developers who thrive on solving challenging problems and building large-scale distributed systems. AWS runs one of the largest networks in the world, and MONA alone owns the full lifecycle of over a million physical devices — driving new innovation in one of the largest data center networks on Earth. Everything we run we build in-house: controllers, software-defined networking, planning software, etc.

Basic qualifications

- 7+ years of non-internship professional software development experience
- 7+ years of programming with at least one software programming language experience
- 7+ years of leading design or architecture (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems experience
- Experience as a mentor, tech lead or leading an engineering team

Preferred qualifications

- 5+ years of full software development life cycle, including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, and operations experience
- Master's degree in computer science or equivalent

- Experience leading the design, automation, deployment, and support of large-scale infrastructure

descriptionHtml:
Du bewirbst dich auf unseren Talent Pool für Logistikpraktika mit Start ab Januar 2027. Durch eine frühzeitige Bewerbung profitierst du von:

* Frühzeitiger Berücksichtigung für verfügbare Positionen
* Bevorzugtem Zugang zu gewünschten Standorten und Startdaten
* Größerer Flexibilität bei der Terminplanung im Interviewprozess

Unser vorläufiger Zeitplan: Interviews beginnen im September, das Role Matching startet voraussichtlich im Oktober. Dieser Zeitplan kann sich je nach geschäftlichem Bedarf ändern.

Bitte beachte: Wir haben verschiedene Möglichkeiten in ganz Deutschland und benötigen Flexibilität bezüglich der Standorte. Wenn du dich für die Stelle bewirbst, gib bitte alle deine bevorzugten Standorte in Deutschland an.
Alle unsere Praktika finden vollständig vor Ort statt.
Amazon Operations ist das Rückgrat der Amazon-Kundenerfahrung. Mit über 50 Logistikzentren, hunderten von Zustellstationen und zehntausenden von Versandmitarbeiter:innen arbeitet das Team zusammen, um Artikel effizient an Kund:innen zu liefern. In den Logistikzentren werden jährlich Millionen von Artikeln kommissioniert und verpackt, während die Zustellteams daran arbeiten, Bestellungen pünktlich an die Kund:innen zu bringen. Sicherheit hat oberste Priorität, und die Betriebskultur ist geprägt von Teamwork, Vielfalt und einer gemeinsamen Arbeitsethik, die das Geschäft reibungslos am Laufen hält. Das Team ist stolz darauf, den Qualitätsservice zu liefern, für den Amazon weltweit bekannt ist.

Hinweis: Du musst zum Starttermin die Arbeitsberechtigung für das Beschäftigungsland haben.


Key job responsibilities
Als Amazon Operations-Praktikant:in hast du die Möglichkeit, deine analytischen Fähigkeiten in wirkungsvollen Projekten anzuwenden, die die Funktionalität und den Service von Logistikzentren, Sortierzentren und Zustellstationen verbessern. Wichtige Aspekte der Rolle umfassen:
• Abschluss von Projekten mit hoher Priorität nach höchstem Standard und Nachweis deiner Fähigkeit, Ergebnisse zu liefern
• Datenanalyse zur Identifizierung operativer Herausforderungen und Verbesserungsmöglichkeiten
• Vorschlagen und Testen von Lösungen in Zusammenarbeit mit dem Team zur Umsetzung der effektivsten Ansätze
• Entwicklung von Kommunikations- und Teamfähigkeiten durch die Zusammenarbeit mit Führungskräften, Stakeholdern und Versandmitarbeiter:innen.
• Bewegung im Gebäude, um mit verschiedenen Teams zu interagieren. Das umfasst aktives Wissenssammeln durch Teilnahme an Aktivitäten wie Vorbesprechungen, Ablaufmeetings und Diskussionen mit dem Führungsteam und Versandmitarbeiter:innen.
• Die Fähigkeit, sich im Arbeitsbereich zu orientieren und zwischen verschiedenen Bereichen zu wechseln, ist für diese Position unerlässlich.
• Flexibilität bei verschiedenen Arbeitszeiten und Schichtmustern nach Bedarf zeigen.
• Möglicher Umzug an den vorgesehenen Arbeitsort.


A day in the life
Unsere Praktika sind Bildungsmöglichkeiten, die es dir als unserer zukünftigen Führungskraft ermöglichen, zu entdecken, wie wir unsere Teams von Versandmitarbeiter:innen führen und entwickeln. Du tauchst in die schnelllebige, komplexe Welt unserer Logistikzentren, Sortierzentren und Zustellstationen ein und erlebst, wie unsere Führungskräfte ihre Teams einsetzen, um Kundenerwartungen zu erfüllen.
Dieses Praktikum versetzt dich ins Herz unserer Abläufe und ermöglicht es dir, den Weg einer Kundenbestellung zu verfolgen. Du erhältst einen realistischen Einblick in die Vollzeitchancen, die dich in unserem Unternehmen erwarten.
Du lernst, wie unsere Führungskräfte eine sichere, produktive Umgebung schaffen und das volle Potenzial ihrer Teams durch effektive Einbindung und Leistungsmanagement-Strategien nutzen. Das ist deine Chance, Fähigkeiten zu entwickeln, die dich zu einer lohnenden Karriere bei Amazon führen werden.


About the team
Praktikant:innen-Community:
• Als Amazon-Praktikant:in bist du Teil einer lebendigen, unterstützenden Community, die dein Wachstum und deine Entwicklung fördert. Du arbeitest mit Praktikant:innen aus der ganzen Welt zusammen, knüpfst Kontakte und nimmst an sozialen Veranstaltungen teil, um deinen Horizont zu erweitern. Du kannst auch spezialisierten Gruppen beitreten, die sich auf Bereiche wie Nachhaltigkeit konzentrieren, um deine vielfältigen Interessen zu erkunden.
Unterstützung:
• Das Praktikumsprogramm bietet ein robustes Unterstützungssystem, einschließlich wöchentlicher Praktikant:innen-Sprechstunden, spezieller IT- und HR-Unterstützung sowie einem Programmteam, das sich deinem Erfolg verschrieben hat. Das stellt sicher, dass du die Anleitung und Hilfe hast, die du zum Gedeihen brauchst.
Lernsessions:
• Exklusive Lernsessions werden deine Fähigkeiten weiter verbessern und dir Zugang zu Amazons modernsten Lernplattformen und der Expertise von Branchenführern gewähren. Diese strukturierten Entwicklungsmöglichkeiten bereiten dich auf den nächsten Schritt in deiner Karriere vor.
Möglichkeiten:
• Nach erfolgreichem Abschluss des Praktikums kannst du für eine Absolvent:innen-Stelle oder ein zweites Praktikum in Betracht gezogen werden, was es dir ermöglicht, deine Reise mit Amazon fortzusetzen. Zusätzlich erhältst du ein wettbewerbsfähiges Monatsgehalt, Umzugsunterstützung und Zugang zu einer Reihe von Mitarbeitervorteilen.
Praktikums-Starttermine über das Jahr:
• Wir stellen Praktikant:innen ein, die jederzeit von Januar bis Juli 2027 anfangen können. Jeden Monat führen wir 1-2 Onboarding-Tage für neue Mitarbeiter:innen durch.

title: 2027 MBA Leadership Development Program (MLDP) Intern
descriptionHtml:
Build What's Next: Your Enterprise Leadership Journey Starts Here

What if your first role after business school put you at the intersection of commerce, product, and AI - with the ownership to build something that didn't exist before? Join Amazon's MBA Leadership Development Program (MLDP), starting with a transformative summer internship where you'll solve real business problems with measurable customer impact.

MLDP Overview
Amazon Stores is becoming an AI-first organization - and the leaders who will shape its future aren't just operators. They're builders. MLDP is an accelerated leadership pipeline that develops product-minded enterprise leaders capable of running businesses while simultaneously reinventing how Amazon serves hundreds of millions of customers.

Your journey begins with a 12-week summer internship, where you'll own a strategic business challenge, work alongside senior leaders, and present your findings in a formal business review. Successful interns transition into the full-time, three-year MLDP - a structured development experience designed to build the commercial judgment, product thinking, and cross-functional influence that define Amazon's next generation of enterprise leaders.

Through rotational experiences spanning business ownership, product, and operations, you'll progressively take on greater scope and complexity. MLDP is more than rotations - it's Enterprise Challenges sponsored by senior leaders, executive mentorship, cohort-based development, and the opportunity to build AI-enabled capabilities and operating mechanisms that create lasting value across Amazon Stores.

Summer Internship Focus
As an MLDP intern, you'll:
- Own a strategic business problem with real P&L impact and present your solution to senior leadership
- Apply data, customer insights, and emerging technologies to identify opportunities others haven't seen
- Collaborate across functions to develop innovative, scalable business solutions
- Build relationships with executive leaders, current MLDP participants, and program alumni
- Experience Amazon's builder culture firsthand where curiosity, ownership, and invention are rewarded

Future MLDP Opportunities
Successful interns may be considered for the full three-year MLDP, which includes:
- Rotational experiences across business ownership, product, and operations - building enterprise leadership breadth
- Enterprise Challenges that put you at the center of Amazon Stores' high-priority business problems
- Executive sponsorship and structured leadership development designed to accelerate your trajectory
- A cohort of peers from the nation's top MBA programs, building careers and connections together
Join us in shaping the future of retail while developing into a next-generation business leader at one of the world's most customer-centric companies.

Key job responsibilities
MLDP seeks builders - leaders with product-minded curiosity, analytical judgment, learning agility, and a long-term orientation toward creating something better. You thrive in ambiguity, ask the right questions, influence across organizations, and see AI as a strategic advantage, not just a productivity tool. You want early P&L accountability, founder-level ownership, and a clear path to enterprise leadership at scale.

- Duration: 12 consecutive weeks

title: Sensor System Engineer (Robotic vision), Amazon Robotics
descriptionHtml:
We are seeking a Sensor System Engineer to join the Machine Vision Systems team at Amazon Robotics. This is a cross-disciplinary Subject Matter Expert (SME) role that bridges the gap between customers, product strategy, and deep technical execution. The ideal candidate thrives at the intersection of systems engineering, product management, and customer engagement, translating real-world needs into actionable sensor solutions for next-generation robotic platforms.

Key job responsibilities
Customer Engagement & Requirements Gathering: Serve as a primary technical point of contact for internal and external customers. Conduct discovery sessions, gather use-case requirements, and translate customer needs into quantifiable technical specifications and design goals.

Product Definition & Roadmap Support: Partner with product management to define product requirements, prioritize features, and shape the sensor product roadmap based on customer feedback, market trends, and technical feasibility.

System Architecture: Contribute to sensor system architecture selections, ensuring designs meet performance, cost, reliability, and integration requirements across mechanical, electrical, and optical domains.

Technology Benchmarking & Competitive Analysis: Evaluate emerging sensing technologies, benchmark against competitive solutions, and identify opportunities to differentiate. Maintain awareness of industry trends, academic research, and market dynamics in robotics sensing (navigation, perception, manipulation).

Technical Challenge Identification: Proactively identify and communicate technical risks and enablement problems for customer applications. Develop mitigation strategies and trade-off assessments to guide engineering selections.

Cross-Functional Collaboration: Work across hardware, firmware, optical, mechanical, electrical, test, and manufacturing teams to ensure cohesive system-level solutions. Communicate effectively across disciplines to align stakeholders on requirements and priorities.


A day in the life
Mornings typically begin with cross-functional standups alongside optical, electrical, and mechanical teams to align on sensor development priorities. Mid-morning involves customer calls — gathering requirements, clarifying use cases, and presenting technical trade-offs. Afternoons shift between benchmarking vying sensor technologies, updating product requirement documents, and collaborating with product managers on roadmap selections. Time is also spent examining market trends, reviewing architecture proposals, and documenting technical challenges that impact customer enablement. The role requires constant context-switching between deep technical analysis and stakeholder communication, ensuring customer needs continuously inform engineering direction.

title: Area Manager Intern – Summer 2027 (ND, SD, NE, KS, MN, IA, WI, IL, MI, IN)
descriptionHtml:
Power that runs the world | Discover careers in Operations
Operations roles at Amazon put you at the center of how things move from a click to a doorstep. You'll help design, improve, and run systems that connect people, products, and places, at scale. You'll take ownership early, work closely with teams to solve real-world challenges, and see the direct results of your decisions as they reach customers every day. Here, the impact of what you build isn't abstract, it's visible, immediate, and meaningful - keeping one of the world's most complex operations moving forward. This is where your journey takes shape through action, responsibility, and the opportunity to grow in many directions.

This is not a corporate, remote or office-based position. This is a ten-week internship (40 hours per week) during the summer of 2027 located within one of Amazon’s fulfillment centers, sort centers, delivery stations or other operations buildings. Amazon is seeking customer focused individuals eager to develop a collaborative leadership style with a team of hourly employees across our Operations network! Our warehouses are fast-paced supply chain environments where standing, walking, and having on-the-production floor conversations are common.

As an Area Manager Intern, you will have the opportunity to learn how to coach, motivate and mentor a team of Amazon associates in a warehouse environment. Amazon provides extensive training and development to become an exceptional people leader. Your main focus will be learning to manage a team as well as developing a summer project in partnership with your site leadership.

Term: 10 weeks

Benefits: Access to Amazon's Medical Advice Line, Employee Assistance Program (EAP), and financial benefits.

Visit www.aboutamazon.com/workplace/facilities to find more information on each of our building types.

Please note we are not able to provide sponsorship now or in the future for these positions. Eligible candidates must have work authorization without employer intervention to be considered.

This posting encompasses all openings in the state(s) listed in title. Site placement is matched by aligning your location preferences with location availability after your interview. Summer relocation and housing assistance provided if eligible.


Key job responsibilities
• Learn to coach, manage and develop a team of 50-100 Amazon Associates.
• Drive standard work and continuous improvement through an intern project.
• Work independently and operate in an autonomous environment.
• Stand/walk during shifts lasting up to 12 hours.
• Willing and able to regularly work shift patterns that include nights, weekends, and/or holidays based on business needs. While shifts vary site to site, most follow a fixed 4-day work week with 3 days off.
• Oversee truck deliveries, handle and sort packages using pallet jacks, operate PIT equipment (at applicable facilities) and step in as needed.
• Work in an environment where the noise level varies.
• Lift up to 49 pounds and frequently push, pull, squat, bend and reach.
• Climb and descend stairs (when applicable).


A day in the life
As an Area Manager intern, no two days look exactly the same, but every shift gives you the chance to learn how to lead a team, solve real problems, and directly impact how millions of customers receive their orders.

Start of Shift: Set the Tone
• Shadow a current Area Manager and begin to:
• Get a handoff from the outgoing manager and review what's carrying over so nothing falls through the cracks.
• Lead a team huddle to kick off the shift. Huddles are used to align on goals, safety priorities, and key focus areas.
• Confirm your team is in place, positioned for success, and ready to go before operations begin.

Middle of Shift: Lead from the Floor
• Walk the floor regularly to stay connected to your team, spot issues early, and keep things running smoothly.
• Drive results across safety, quality, and productivity — balancing all three in real time.
• Adjust staffing and resources as volume and priorities shift throughout the day.
• Coach and develop your team members, respond to challenges as they come up, and partner with support teams to remove roadblocks.
• Keep peers and leadership informed on how the shift is tracking and flag risks before they become problems.
• Develop your internship project.

End of Shift: Close Strong
• Do a final walkthrough to make sure your area is clean, organized, and set up for the next team's success.
• Review your shift's performance data and capture what went well and what to improve
• Hand off to the incoming manager with a clear picture of priorities, open items, and next steps.
• Wrap up any remaining administrative tasks so you leave the shift with a clean slate.
Every shift, you'll see the direct results of your leadership: from the energy of your team to the packages that reach customers' doorsteps. This is where your decisions have real, visible impact.

title: Operations Specialist, Retail Origin Ops
descriptionHtml:
At Amazon, we're working to be the most customer-centric company on Earth. To get there, we need exceptionally talented, bright, and driven people.

Amazon's Retail Origin Operations team is at the frontline of our global supply chain — overseeing freight movement across 120+ origin ports to 70+ destination ports, serving marketplaces in the US, EU, JP, CA, MX, AU, SG, TR, and MENA regions. As cross-border trade volume grows and business complexity increases, we are seeking an Operations Specialist to help manage logistics service provider (LSP) performance and ensure the seamless execution of retail direct import bookings from origin to destinations.

This role sits within the Global Logistics organization. We are looking for candidates with a strong foundation in international freight operations, proven ability to manage LSPs and carriers through data-driven mechanisms, and a continuous improvement mindset. You will operate across ocean, LCL, rail, and air modes, working with partners including Origin Cargo Management service providers, NVOCCs, and LCL service providers. The ideal candidate thrives in ambiguity, takes ownership of outcomes, and brings both analytical rigor and collaborative energy to everything they do.

Key job responsibilities
As an Operations Specialist, you will be responsible for managing retail booking processing and logistic service provider management at origin including:
1. Daily Operations & Exception Management: Execute assigned tasks per SOPs, resolve exceptions within SLA, and apply sound judgment when no existing procedure applies.
2.LSP Performance Management: Build mechanisms to track and improve logistics service provider performance — optimize KPIs, conduct root cause analysis, and own corrective actions through to resolution.
3. Carrier & Partner Collaboration: Work directly with origin LSPs and internal supportive functions to resolve operational issues and protect the experience of retail selling partners and internal stakeholders.
4. Risk & Compliance Handling: Assess compliance risks, surface roadblocks early, and escalate with clarity — particularly in regulatory or time-sensitive shipment scenarios.
5. Process Standardization & Kaizen: Drive standardization and Kaizen initiatives across carrier and LSP networks to improve logistics quality and reduce cost at scale.
6. Cross-Functional Process Improvement: Serve as a process subject matter expert, partnering with internal teams and external stakeholders to design and implement operational improvements across the supply chain.
7. New Initiative Support: Contribute to strategic programs and business launches, advancing operational excellence goals across speed, cost, and service quality as team scope expands.

Basic qualifications

- Bachelor's degree or equivalent
- 1+ years of logistics, transportation, supply chain, import/export operations, or data entry/data administration experience
- Experience influencing multiple stakeholders and leading cross functional teams across geographies and business units
- Experience demonstrating strong analytical abilities and confidence in the use of data
- Experience working proactively and independently, meeting deadlines, and delivering on projects and tasks
- Experience dealing effectively with customers during problem resolution and operating efficiently under pressure
- Experience in English-language communication skills, both written and verbal

Preferred qualifications

- Experience managing operations and customer service teams with extensive knowledge of Logistics

title: HR Business Partner, Worldwide Grocery Stores
descriptionHtml:
En nuestra búsqueda de ser el mejor empleador, los equipos globales de Recursos Humanos —conocidos como People eXperience and Technology (PXT)— impulsan el éxito del negocio fomentando una cultura segura, inclusiva e innovadora. El HR Business Partner es responsable de la excelencia operativa y la salud organizacional en los centros asignados, actuando como colaborador/a individual en estrecha alianza con los equipos locales y los equipos de liderazgo del centro.

Este rol fortalecerá la cultura y obtendrá resultados de negocio traduciendo las prioridades organizacionales en planes de acción, tomando decisiones basadas en datos y colaborando con los líderes del campus para mejorar la experiencia de las personas trabajadoras. Este rol es responsable de la experiencia de las personas trabajadoras, siendo responsable de los mecanismos de Feedback a nivel de centro, los programas de reconocimiento y los estándares que configuran la confianza, el compromiso y el desempeño.

Se requiere presencia física en las instalaciones de Amazon, con movilidad para dar soporte a múltiples centros dentro de la región asignada.

Key job responsibilities
• Fomentar la comunicación bidireccional entre personas trabajadoras y líderes a través de mecanismos de Feedback como la voz del asociado, mesas redondas y recorridos por la planta.
• Ejecutar y hacer seguimiento de estrategias de compromiso y programas de reconocimiento, incluyendo la planificación presupuestaria y las actividades de reconocimiento.
• Construir un entorno donde las personas se sientan seguras e incluidas, garantizando prácticas de talento equitativas.
• Mantener una presencia significativa en planta en todo el centro, recopilando información e identificando señales tempranas de desvinculación.
Excelencia Operativa y Estándares del Centro
• Realizar recorridos regulares por el centro para evaluar las condiciones del lugar de trabajo y mantener los estándares de las instalaciones en línea con los estándares de Amazon.
• Colaborar con los líderes del centro y los equipos de seguridad para garantizar la ejecución consistente de los programas de seguridad.
• Liderar iniciativas comunitarias en el/los centro/s, colaborando con los equipos de Política Pública y Relaciones Públicas.
• Mejorar la efectividad del centro identificando patrones sistémicos, abordando causas raíz y garantizando una aplicación consistente y equitativa de las políticas.
• Toma de Decisiones Basada en Datos y Tecnología
• Utilizar análisis de datos para identificar tendencias emergentes, anticipar desafíos e implementar soluciones proactivas.
• Impulsar la adopción de soluciones tecnológicas de HR, IA y herramientas de autoservicio, manteniendo un servicio de alto contacto en los momentos críticos. Liderazgo Estratégico PXT
• Colaborar con el equipo de liderazgo del centro para equilibrar las necesidades operativas con los valores y las prioridades de personas de Amazon.
• Orientar a los lideres de negocio sobre prácticas eficaces de gestión de personas, incluyendo Feedback de desempeño, desarrollo del equipo y asuntos de relaciones laborales.
• Apoyar la implementación del cambio reforzando los mensajes, abordando la resistencia y ayudando a los líderes a traducir el cambio en rutinas locales.
• Ejecutar los procesos clave de PXT construyendo confianza e influencia a través del conocimiento del negocio.

A day in the life
Tu día combina pensamiento estratégico y toma de decisiones basada en datos. Aprovecharás análisis avanzados y herramientas habilitadas por IA para identificar tendencias, anticipar las necesidades del negocio y desarrollar soluciones que mejoren la experiencia en el lugar de trabajo. Desde orientar a los equipos de liderazgo en la gestión de la plantilla hasta impulsar la excelencia en los procesos de HR, colaborarás con los Field Leaders en los objetivos operativos y la efectividad del equipo.
Mantendrás una fuerte presencia en planta, construyendo alianzas en todos los niveles y contribuyendo a mejoras significativas a través de recorridos por el centro, sesiones de Feedback y proyectos estratégicos. El éxito proviene de tu capacidad para gestionar la dinámica organizacional, liderar iniciativas de cambio y tomar decisiones de alto criterio en situaciones ambiguas.

- Experiencia apoyando y/o liderando procesos centrados en las personas trabajadoras como incorporación, beneficios, investigaciones, formación y/o gestión del talento

- Experiencia en entornos operativos (fabricación, distribución o similares)
- Capacidad para formar y apoyar a otras personas en el uso de tecnologías de HR y plataformas digitales, con foco en aumentar la adopción y mejorar la experiencia de usuario

title: Sr Automation Engineer, EMA5 RME
descriptionHtml:
Operations is at the heart of everything Amazon does, and automation is one of the ways we optimise our processes. As an Automation Engineer, you’ll make sure that our automated systems are working at their best so that our customers get their orders on time. By exploring data on everything from control systems to sensors, you’ll maximise the availability of equipment at your sites. This role puts you at the forefront of Amazon’s emerging technology to solve complex productivity challenges.

Key job responsibilities
Monitor, troubleshoot and repair issues with key systems
Work with the EU Controls network to monitor Material Handling Equipment (MHE) metrics
Provide data visualisations of troubleshooting to internal stakeholders
Own or actively participate in continuous improvement projects run by the EU Controls network
Work with different departments to ensure all systems are correctly documented and that accurate backup libraries are maintained
Work with global colleagues to install and commission new equipment
Support other sites in the EU Controls network as needed
Interpret mechanical and electrical drawings, and develop improvement strategies for code conforming to IEC 61131-3

A day in the life
As a Senior Automation Engineer, you’ll be the site expert when it comes to keeping key automated systems running smoothly. You’ll be working with our automation machinery, from conveyors to sortation systems, and ensuring they’re working efficiently. If something has gone wrong or can be done better, you’ll take the lead in coming up with and implementing a solution.

You’ll also share your expertise with your close colleagues. You’ll be keeping your Engineering Technicians up to date with device troubleshooting and preventative maintenance control training, so that your team can keep our automation systems in order.

About the team
Our Reliability Maintenance Engineering or RME team keep our equipment performing at its best. We're a technically minded team, made up of excellent team players and guided by experienced leaders. We work together to maintain, troubleshoot and repair equipment across our global network of fulfilment centres. Some of our people are leaders, who oversee the team as they work on exciting technology – some of which only exists at Amazon.

From installing automated packaging systems to overseeing the general maintenance of a site to repairing key distribution equipment, our team handles most aspects of Amazon’s technical side. This includes keeping buildings legally compliant, so everyone is safe, and our sites are operating at maximum efficiency. There are lots of opportunities for progression, both within the RME team and more widely across Amazon.

Everything we do focuses on reducing downtime in Amazon’s crucial operations sites, so customers get their orders on time. We often work during early or late hours to carry out maintenance with minimal disruption, including night shifts. If we spot a better way to do something, we have the skills and the opportunity to develop and introduce completely new processes or cutting-edge tech like Amazon Robotics and our Complex Item Sorter.

Basic qualifications

- Work a flexible schedule/shift/work area, including weekends, nights, and/or holidays
- Travel up to 80% of the time
- Experience with PLC-controlled automation
- Relevant experience with PLC-controlled automation and issue diagnosis in a continuous process or production environment
- Relevant experience supporting different conveyors and sortation systems
- Relevant experience dealing with material handling, flow and capacity visualisation, and monitoring
- Experience with at least one of the following tools:
- EthernetIP, Profinet, Profibus and AS-i or other fieldbus networks
- VFDs, safety gateways and input and output devices
- Advanced proficiency in verbal and written English and local language

Preferred qualifications

- Master's degree, or Six Sigma Black Belt certification
- Experience with creating automated alarms, reports and KPI metrics for plant management
- Experience using relational databases (SQL experience)
- Experience leading controls in manufacturing or complex industrial environments
- Experience identifying, maintaining, troubleshooting, and modifying Motor Controls including motor starters, Variable Frequency Drives, DC drives, and standard electrical components
- Experience interpreting and modifying mechanical and electrical drawings
- A degree in computer science, electrical engineering, industrial electronics or another technical subject
- Experience working within ISO 13849 and ISO 62061 frameworks
- Project management experience with multiple frameworks such as Agile and Waterfall
- Experience of Six Sigma, data analysis or process improvement techniques

title: Sr Sales Specialist Databases, Specialists Team Germany, Switzerland and CEE, Specialists Team Germany, Switzerland and CEE
descriptionHtml:
At Amazon, we are working to be the most customer-centric company on earth. To get there, we need exceptionally talented, bright, and driven people. Amazon is continually evolving and is a place where motivated employees thrive and also where employee ownership and accountability lead to meaningful results. We are seeking a customer- obsessed, highly motivated Database Specialist to join our Database Specialist team in Germany. This is a domain specialist position for someone who can own the full database conversation, from legacy commercial database estates through migration and modernization, all the way to purpose- built and open-source architectures on AWS.

Key job responsibilities
Own the end-to-end database conversation from commercial database migration (Oracle, SQL Server, DB2), to open-source conversion (PostgreSQL, MySQL), to purpose-built non-relational databases (key-value, document, graph, in-memory, time-series).
Drive Database GTM strategy.
Define and execute account-level go-to-market plans for AWS database technologies, leveraging the broader AWS sales team and partner ecosystem.
Be the domain authority. Act as the primary Database specialist within your accounts, leading all customer engagements related to database platform
strategy, migration planning, and workload modernization.
Bridge technical and business stakeholders. Translate complex database migration risks, TCO models, and architectural trade-offs into compelling business narratives for Line of Business and C-suite leaders.
Commercial database conversions.
Help customers reduce dependency on expensive commercial database licenses by identifying migration paths, proving out open-source alternatives, and demonstrating the value of purpose-built databases for specific workload patterns.
Build and innovate. Co-develop GTM motions for new product launches and contribute customer insights directly to AWS product teams to influence the database services roadmap.
Leverage the partner ecosystem. Collaborate with database-focused partners and global/regional system integrators to design and deliver database migration and modernization
programs at scale.

A day in the life
The Database Specialist Team is composed of deep domain experts embedded within account teams across Germany. We work at the intersection of technology and business helping customers think big about their data strategy and delivering the specialized expertise needed to make it real. We are responsible for account planning, opportunity identification, and pursuit. We stay closely connected to our customers and bring valuable field insights back to our product teams, directly strengthening the AWS database roadmap. Our team thrives when customers are ready to migrate and modernize their most critical database workloads.

About the team
Diverse Experiences
Amazon values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

Why AWS
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

Work/Life Balance
We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why flexible work hours and arrangements are part of our culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud.

Inclusive Team Culture
Here at AWS, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Our employee-led affinity groups foster a culture of inclusion that empower us to be proud of our differences. Ongoing events and learning experiences, including our Conversations on Race and Ethnicity (CORE) and AmazeCon (gender diversity) conferences, inspire us to never stop embracing our uniqueness.

Mentorship and Career Growth
We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Basic qualifications

title: Area Manager Intern - Summer 2027 (California), University Recruiting
descriptionHtml:
Power that runs the world | Discover careers in Operations

Operations roles at Amazon put you at the center of how things move from a click to a doorstep. You'll help design, improve, and run systems that connect people, products, and places, at scale. You'll take ownership early, work closely with teams to solve real-world challenges, and see the direct results of your decisions as they reach customers every day. Here, the impact of what you build isn't abstract, it's visible, immediate, and meaningful - keeping one of the world's most complex operations moving forward. This is where your journey takes shape through action, responsibility, and the opportunity to grow in many directions.

This is not a corporate, remote or office-based position. This is a ten-week internship (40 hours per week) during the summer of 2027 located within one of Amazon’s fulfillment centers, sort centers, delivery stations or other operations buildings. Amazon is seeking customer focused individuals eager to develop a collaborative leadership style with a team of hourly employees across our Operations network! Our warehouses are fast-paced supply chain environments where standing, walking, and having on-the-production floor conversations are common.

As an Area Manager Intern, you will have the opportunity to learn how to coach, motivate and mentor a team of Amazon associates in a warehouse environment. Amazon provides extensive training and development to become an exceptional people leader. Your main focus will be learning to manage a team as well as developing a summer project in partnership with your site leadership.

Term: 10 weeks

Benefits: Access to Amazon's Medical Advice Line, Employee Assistance Program (EAP), and financial benefits.

Visit www.aboutamazon.com/workplace/facilities to find more information on each of our building types.

Please note we are not able to provide sponsorship now or in the future for these positions. Eligible candidates must have work authorization without employer intervention to be considered.

This posting encompasses all openings in the state(s) listed in title. Site placement is matched by aligning your location preferences with location availability after your interview. Summer relocation and housing assistance provided if eligible.


Key job responsibilities
• Learn to coach, manage and develop a team of 50-100 Amazon Associates.
• Drive standard work and continuous improvement through an intern project.
• Work independently and operate in an autonomous environment.
• Stand/walk during shifts lasting up to 12 hours.
• Willing and able to regularly work shift patterns that include nights, weekends, and/or holidays based on business needs. While shifts vary site to site, most follow a fixed 4-day work week with 3 days off.
• Oversee truck deliveries, handle and sort packages using pallet jacks, operate PIT equipment (at applicable facilities) and step in as needed.
• Work in an environment where the noise level varies.
• Lift up to 49 pounds and frequently push, pull, squat, bend and reach.
• Climb and descend stairs (when applicable).


A day in the life
As an Area Manager intern, no two days look exactly the same, but every shift gives you the chance to learn how to lead a team, solve real problems, and directly impact how millions of customers receive their orders.

Start of Shift: Set the Tone
• Shadow a current Area Manager and begin to:
• Get a handoff from the outgoing manager and review what's carrying over so nothing falls through the cracks.
• Lead a team huddle to kick off the shift. Huddles are used to align on goals, safety priorities, and key focus areas.
• Confirm your team is in place, positioned for success, and ready to go before operations begin.

Middle of Shift: Lead from the Floor
• Walk the floor regularly to stay connected to your team, spot issues early, and keep things running smoothly.
• Drive results across safety, quality, and productivity — balancing all three in real time.
• Adjust staffing and resources as volume and priorities shift throughout the day.
• Coach and develop your team members, respond to challenges as they come up, and partner with support teams to remove roadblocks.
• Keep peers and leadership informed on how the shift is tracking and flag risks before they become problems.
• Develop your internship project.

End of Shift: Close Strong
• Do a final walkthrough to make sure your area is clean, organized, and set up for the next team's success.
• Review your shift's performance data and capture what went well and what to improve
• Hand off to the incoming manager with a clear picture of priorities, open items, and next steps.
• Wrap up any remaining administrative tasks so you leave the shift with a clean slate.

Every shift, you'll see the direct results of your leadership: from the energy of your team to the packages that reach customers' doorsteps. This is where your decisions have real, visible impact.

- Currently enrolled in a bachelor’s degree program with all requirements anticipated to be completed between December 2027 and August 2028.

- Strong communication skills, both verbal and written.
- Excellent customer service and interpersonal skills.
- Currently enrolled in a Bachelor's program for Supply Chain, Business/Management, Engineering or another related field.

title: Data Center Engineering Operations Technician
descriptionHtml:
How would you like to be a part of Earth’s most customer-centric company? You would work with teams of front-line responders who support the operations of some of the world’s most powerful data centers. Our Data Center Engineering Operations team maintain and operate our critical infrastructure systems so that they are prepared to stand up against any situation.

AWS has the world’s largest cloud computing portfolio. As an Amazonian you will work in some of the most sophisticated, safe, and secure data centers in the world. Our Engineering Operations Technicians (EOT’s) help keep them that way by working with the brightest minds from around the globe to help test and implement the newest technology and work practices to meet the demands of a changing market.

We have a passion for learning and evolving, it’s how we have helped define ourselves as leaders in the industry. Let’s work hard, have fun, and make history!

Key job responsibilities
- Daily building rounds to monitor and record information from electrical, mechanical, and fire/life safety equipment to ensure 24/7 reliability and availability
- Monitor Building Management Systems (BMS) and Electrical Power Management System (EPMS)
- Assist in troubleshooting of facility and rack-level events within internal Service Level Agreements (SLA)
- Perform rack installs and rack decommissioning within internal SLA
- Perform PM, troubleshooting, root cause analysis, and repair of electrical and mechanical equipment
- Technical writing to support change management program
- Monitor daily work requests and manage to resolution, and execute projects from conception to completion
- On-site support of contractors, sub-contractors and vendors, ensuring that all work performed is in accordance with established practices, procedures & local legislation
- Work schedule changes depending on specific site needs. Shifts can be up to 12-hours and may rotate on a predefined schedule. Some locations have on-call rotations.
- Role may support more than one location/site.

Work Schedule:
Our Data Centers operate 24/7 and require on-site presence. This position offers two shift schedule options:

Option 1: Weekend Rotation
- Days Worked: Sunday - Tuesday, plus every other Saturday
- Weekly Pattern: Alternates between 3-day and 4-day work weeks
- Shift Hours: 5:30am - 6:00pm (day shift) OR 5:30pm - 6:00am (night shift)

Option 2: Weekday Rotation
- Days Worked: Wednesday - Friday, plus every other Saturday
- Weekly Pattern: Alternates between 3-day and 4-day work weeks
- Shift Hours: 5:30am - 6:00pm (day shift) OR 5:30pm - 6:00am (night shift)

Both schedules follow a rotating pattern where you'll work 3 days one week and 4 days the following week.

Overtime & Pay
- Overtime: Time and a half after 40 hours per week
- Night Shift Differential: 13% additional pay (6:00pm - 6:00am shifts)
- Maximum Hours: 60 hours per week in total (up to 20 hours of overtime)

Physical Requirements:
- Willingness and demonstrated ability to work in the following physical conditions with reasonable accommodations:
- Regularly lift and/or move up to 39 pounds independently
- Participate in group lifts for 40+ pounds
- Maintain balance and perform construction tasks while on a ladder
- Regularly walk, use hands and fingers, handle or feel, reach with hands and arms, stoop, kneel, crouch or crawl, climb stairs, twist, bend, work above shoulders, grasp, carry, push and pull objects into position
- Work in an environment requiring provided ear protection

A day in the life
This role acts as Amazon’s front line when it comes to hands-on electrical and mechanical equipment preventative maintenance (PM) and troubleshooting, reporting to a site’s Data Center Facility Manager (FM). They will maintain, operate, and troubleshoot mission-critical data center facility equipment including stand-by diesel generators and related fuel systems, 3 phase electrical systems such as switchgear, UPS units, PDUs, and wet cell batteries and associated systems. Mechanical equipment includes CRAHU units, centrifugal chillers, cooling towers, water systems, air handlers and associated systems, pumps, and motors. Additional support equipment is included in the scope of the role which includes fire/life safety equipment, building automation systems, and general facilities equipment.

About the team
AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

Why AWS?
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

Diverse Experiences
AWS values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

Inclusive Team Culture
Here at AWS, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Our employee-led affinity groups foster a culture of inclusion that empower us to be proud of our differences. Ongoing events and learning experiences, including our Conversations on Race and Ethnicity (CORE) and AmazeCon conferences, inspire us to never stop embracing our uniqueness.

Mentorship & Career Growth
We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Work/Life Balance
We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud.

Basic qualifications

- Work shifts longer than eight hours in duration
- 2+ years of practical experience in electrical systems, mechanical systems, HVAC, and/or fire suppression systems

Preferred qualifications

- Knowledge of network design and layout as well as low voltage (copper/ fiber) cabling
- Experience in data center engineering

title: Sr. Hardware Technical Program Manager, Product Sustaining, Ring & Blink Devices (L6)
descriptionHtml:
Ring & Blink Products & Delivery Org is seeking a Sr. Technical Program Manager to join our Product Sustaining team. You will own end-to-end program execution for sustaining hardware initiatives across Ring and Blink's mass production devices — from post-ramp through end-of-life. This includes leading engineering changes, second-source qualifications, cost-down programs, new SKU development, and technical/operational issue resolution across global cross-functional teams, Contract Manufacturers (CMs), and 3rd-party labs to ensure long-term product quality, supply resilience, and customer experience.

At Ring/Blink, Sr. TPMs operate with AI-native fluency — using AI tools as a core part of how you plan, execute, communicate, and deliver. You will set AI-native standards for the sustaining function, build reusable workflows the team adopts, and measure success by customer impact. You own every output you ship, AI-assisted or not.

The ideal candidate brings experience leading complex hardware sustaining programs, navigating system and supply trade-offs, and driving continuous improvement — while leveraging AI to multiply team effectiveness.

Key job responsibilities
- Program Ownership: Own end-to-end sustaining program management for Ring/Blink devices — from mass production through EOL. Manage multiple concurrent programs across the portfolio.
- Cross-Functional Execution: Lead Engineering, Operations, Quality, Supply Chain, and CMs through engineering changes, PRQ, 2nd-source qualifications, and new SKU development. Build schedules, track milestones, and ensure on-time delivery aligned to business priorities.
- Engineering Change & 2nd-Source: Facilitate intake reviews and impact assessments. Drive 2nd-source programs end-to-end — datasheet comparison, test plan development, production validation, and cut-in monitoring — to strengthen supply resilience.
- Supply Risk & Cost-Down: Proactively mitigate material risks (shortages, EOL, single-source exposure). Drive cost-down through component re-selection, process optimization, and alternate qualification to prevent line-down.
- Quality & Field Performance: Monitor field metrics (returns, failure rates, complaints); drive root-cause analysis and corrective actions. Close the loop from field failures back to engineering and suppliers for systemic improvement.
- Stakeholder Communication: Deliver concise program health updates to leadership. Mentor junior TPMs; drive process and tooling improvements that raise team execution standards.
- AI-Native Practice: Design workflows with AI embedded from the start — automated status generation, risk detection, and reusable tooling (reports, scorecards, issue pipelines) the team adopts. Develop expertise in at least one AI domain relevant to TPM work.

A day in the life
You manage 5–8 concurrent sustaining programs across the Ring/Blink portfolio. In a typical week you're reviewing AI-flagged supply risk alerts, driving a 2nd-source PRQ test plan with your engineering counterpart, coordinating with Operation team on a component shortage mitigation, leading an intake review for a new cost-down request, and reviewing the auto-generated sustaining portfolio dashboard before your leadership read-out. You balance reactive issue resolution with proactive quality and cost improvement — and you're continuously building AI workflows that automate the routine so you and the team can focus on decisions, strategy, and customer impact.

About the team
The Ring & Blink Product Sustaining HW TPM team ensures that our shipped devices continue to deliver high-quality performance throughout their lifecycle. We manage engineering changes, qualify alternate components, drive cost optimization, and resolve field quality issues across the full Ring and Blink device portfolio — cameras and video doorbells. Our team operates in Taipei, working closely with engineering in the US and Taiwan, CMs across Asia, and cross-functional partners globally.

- 7+ years of technical product or program management experience
- 7+ years of working directly with engineering teams experience
- 5+ years of technical program management working directly with software engineering teams experience
- Experience managing programs across cross functional teams, building processes and coordinating release schedules
- Experience coordinating with contract manufacturers or ODMs in Asia
- Strong communication skills in English & Chinese

Preferred qualifications

- Bachelor's degree in engineering, computer science or equivalent
- 5+ years of project management disciplines including scope, schedule, budget, quality, along with risk and critical path management experience
- Experience managing projects across cross functional teams, building sustainable processes and coordinating release schedules
- Experience with IP cameras, video doorbells, IoT devices, or similar connected consumer products
- Experience driving cost-down initiatives (component re-selection, process optimization, supplier negotiation)

title: Applied Science Manager, Advertising Trust
descriptionHtml:
Amazon Ads delivers advertising experiences across Amazon's owned-and-operated properties and third-party networks, reaching hundreds of millions of customers worldwide. Within Amazon Ads, Advertising Trust is the science-first organization responsible for ensuring every ad shown to customers meets Amazon's content policies — at massive scale, across all ad formats and global marketplaces.
The Ads Trust Science team builds the ML systems that automate content moderation decisions: multimodal classification, retrieval-based labeling, LLM reasoning, and agentic self-improvement architectures. This requires inventing new approaches at the intersection of computer vision, NLP, information retrieval, and generative AI.
We are seeking an Applied Science Manager to lead a team of applied scientists building next-generation content moderation intelligence. You will own the science roadmap for one of the highest-impact automation programs in Amazon Advertising, defining how multimodal content understanding, retrieval-first classification, and LLM-based reasoning combine into a production system that serves global advertising at scale.

Key job responsibilities
* Lead a team of applied scientists working across multimodal ML (vision-language models, video understanding), large-scale retrieval systems (embedding-based similarity and deduplication), and generative AI (LLM-based policy reasoning, knowledge distillation, agentic architectures, reinforcement learning).
* Define the science strategy for ads trust.
* Own end-to-end delivery of ML solutions: problem formulation, offline experimentation, online A/B testing, and production deployment. Your models directly move automation and defect metrics reported to senior leadership.
* Build and grow scientists — hire, mentor, and develop team members. Raise the science bar through structured review processes and a publication culture within Amazon.
* Partner with engineering, product, and operations teams to translate science investments into measurable automation improvements. Influence roadmaps across dependent teams.
* Communicate science strategy and results to senior leadership through narratives, technical deep-dives, and roadmap documents.

Basic qualifications

- 8+ years of applied research experience
- 4+ years of scientists or machine learning engineers management experience
- 4+ yrs in managing team of 5-15 members

Preferred qualifications

- Experience building production ML systems at Internet scale, especially involving multimodal deep learning, generative AI, or large-scale retrieval
- Track record of delivering automation or classification systems with measurable business impact
- Experience with content moderation, trust & safety, or policy enforcement systems
- Publications in top-tier ML/AI venues (NeurIPS, ICML, CVPR, KDD, ACL, AAAI)
- Experience with LLMs (fine-tuning, distillation, RLHF, prompt engineering)
- Demonstrated ability to define and drive science roadmaps that influence product and business strategy
