You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

AWS is seeking a High Voltage Commissioning Engineer to become part of a AMER’s Amazon Commissioning (ACx) team, responsible for the commissioning and continuous innovation of the Medium Voltage and High Voltage infrastructure associated with our rapidly expanding data center foot print. Successful candidates shall be willing to travel and will be based in Herndon VA.

The responsibilities of the ACx Commissioning Engineer (CxE) include, but are not limited to, oversight and coordination of multi-discipline division of work related to pre-commissioning and commissioning of Amazon critical infrastructure construction and special projects. The CxE is responsible for managing and supporting vendors, providing multi-discipline input into the scheduling, design and planning of projects to contractors and other teams involved. Systems includes low, medium and high voltage power systems, Generators, UPS, HVAC, Chilled Water, BMS, EPMS and AWS proprietary systems.

In addition, the CxE will review all multi-discipline commissioning documents to ensure they are compliant with the basis of design, specifications and standards of the project. The CxE will lead concurrent projects to meet delivery schedule while maintaining compliance to health and safety, policies, standards and finances in all projects. The CxE also audits commissioning activities to ensure compliance with environmental, quality, safety and commissioning requirements, reporting to the ACx Regional Manager on commissioning progress and metrics for assigned projects.

title: Senior Software Development Engineer, Advertiser Experience, Amazon Ads, DVA Global Ads
descriptionHtml:
Advertising is undergoing a transformation, and Amazon Demand Side Platform (ADSP) is at the center of it. We are replacing traditional campaign workflows with AI-powered, agentic experiences that help advertisers plan, launch, and optimize Display, Video, and Audio campaigns more effectively. If you want to shape how programmatic advertising works for brands that collectively manage billions of dollars in annual ad spend, this is the role for you.

As a Senior Software Development Engineer on our engineering team, you will own the design and delivery of products that simplify complex advertiser workflows and unlock new capabilities across the full ad stack. You will partner closely with Sales, Go-to-Market, and cross-functional product and engineering teams to turn ambitious ideas into production systems — rapidly prototyping, iterating, and shipping to keep Amazon competitive in the worldwide advertising market.

Key job responsibilities
Design and deliver full-stack software systems that power the next generation of advertiser experiences on ADSP, taking projects from concept through production with rapid prototyping and iterative releases.
Own your team's architectural direction and technical standards, ensuring designs are well-integrated across the broader ad stack and built to scale with growing advertiser demand.
Collaborate with Sales, Go-to-Market, product, and partner engineering teams to translate advertiser needs into technical solutions that measurably improve campaign setup time and performance.
Evaluate and integrate generative AI tools and techniques into advertiser workflows, identifying where intelligent automation can reduce manual steps and create new value.
Mentor engineers on the team through design reviews, code reviews, and hands-on guidance, raising the quality bar for testing, documentation, and operational practices.

A day in the life
You might start your morning reviewing a prototype you shipped the previous day, incorporating feedback from a Go-to-Market partner who tested a new AI-driven campaign workflow. By midday you are deep in a design review with fellow engineers, debating the right integration points across the ad stack. After lunch you pair with a teammate on a tricky service boundary, then wrap up by pushing code and updating your team's operational runbooks. You balance hands-on coding with cross-team collaboration, keeping a clear line of sight from advertiser pain points to the software you ship.

About the team
Our team within Amazon Advertising builds the ADSP products that tens of thousands of advertisers rely on to reach customers across Amazon properties and third-party websites and apps. The team includes full-stack and backend engineers, applied scientists, product managers, and UX designers working together on campaign management, audience targeting, and reporting systems. We are investing in AI-driven experiences that move advertisers from manual, rules-based workflows to intelligent, agentic solutions. If you are excited about building large-scale advertising systems and applying AI to real advertiser problems, we would love to hear from you.

title: Kernel / Hypervisor Engineer, Firecracker
descriptionHtml:
Join us at AWS Lambda in building global scale compute platforms. We focus on serverless & container virtualization technologies, on trusted compute, and on server fleet tooling. We invent, build, and own building blocks that are the foundation of the cloud. This is an exciting opportunity for you to create new products and services of an innovative team that feels like a start-up!
We are looking for a new teammate who is enthusiastic, curious, empathic, motivated, reliable, with a good sense of ownership, and a drive to invent. In this role, you will work on Firecracker [1], an open source virtualization technology that is purpose-built for creating and managing secure, multi-tenant container and function-based services that provide serverless operational models. . Firecracker is deployed globally as part of AWS Lambda [2], Aurora D-SQL, and other AWS services. Firecracker is also integrated by 10+ teams beyond AWS as part of their platforms [3]. Firecracker has an ambitious multi-year roadmap of tackling impactful and interesting opportunities in the quickly expanding ephemeral compute space - come help us make history!

Your main goal will be to create long-term customer value. You will: work to understand our customers' needs and engineer new features to meet them; own and automate operations; contribute new ideas and methods to continuously improve quality and development efficiency; innovate in the area of ephemeral compute platforms; and be a maintainer of the Firecracker open source project. This position also involves on-call responsibilities, which is typically done once every 8 weeks. We strive to keep this down and ensure our systems are fault tolerant. Our team values work-life balance and we respect each others time.

At Amazon, we are dedicated to making new team members feel welcome and included. We are a team that strives to grow each other through task assignments, mentorship, and trainings. As an Amazonian, you’ll work with some of the most talented engineers in our industry. We believe in attracting, developing and retaining talent from diverse backgrounds. We value different perspectives and looking for team players who are working effectively with teams of diverse peers.

title: Area Manager II
descriptionHtml:

We are looking for motivated, customer-focused individuals who want to join our team as an Area Manager. You will also play a key role in maintaining our customer expectations to ensure customer orders are delivered at the right time, to the right location.

descriptionHtml:

title: Security Engineer II, AWS Security Corporate Response
descriptionHtml:
AWS Corporate Security Response is looking for a Security Engineer who thrives at the intersection of hands-on incident response and intelligent automation. You must think like both an attacker and a defender — understanding adversary tradecraft to detect, investigate, and disrupt threats across Amazon's corporate infrastructure at massive scale.

You'll investigate active threats — malware campaigns, phishing attacks, credential compromise, and novel attack patterns — while simultaneously shaping an agentic investigation platform that scales our response capability beyond what any human team could achieve alone.

You will independently lead security investigations from detection through containment and remediation. You'll extract IOCs, perform host forensics, scope impact across multiple data sources, check for lateral movement, and drive security issues to resolution — documenting every step as the investigation unfolds. You'll also serve as a demanding customer and quality owner of our AI-powered investigation platform, authoring the investigation user stories that define how autonomous agents analyze threats, designing the guardrails that keep them safe, and validating that automated output meets the same standard a skilled human investigator would produce.

When you identify gaps in our capabilities, you won't wait — you'll quickly design and build tooling that enables programmatic automation at scale, then feed those patterns into the next generation of autonomous investigation.

Key job responsibilities
* Lead High Severity security investigations end-to-end: acknowledge, investigate with depth (not speed), document as you go, and own through resolution
* Triage High Severity candidates — promote decisively when indicators are clear, downgrade with documented rationale when they're not
* Analyze open source threat intelligence — these reports contain temporal IOCs that decay with age, making rapid validation and proactive blocking critical
* Author and validate agent investigation user stories, ensuring autonomous investigations match human-quality rigor
* Design and test guardrails and policies — think about how attackers would evade detection, how edge cases produce incorrect results, and how agents might fail in ways developers didn't anticipate
* Build tactical scripts, detection rules, and response automations that address immediate operational gaps — then drive their transition into scalable agentic capabilities
* Participate in a global on-call rotation: own the queue for your shift, monitor operational health, and maintain readiness
* Execute clean shift handoffs: document active investigations, flag anomalies observed during your shift, and explicitly transfer ticket ownership

About the team
CorpSec Response operates 24/7 as a global, follow-the-sun team protecting Amazon's corporate infrastructure. We combine deep human expertise with leading autonomous investigation capabilities. Our engineers are hands-on investigators who also shape the AI systems that augment their work — creating a unique feedback loop between human security expertise and machine-scale automation.

Inclusive Team Culture
We are committed to building a diverse and inclusive team. Amazon's culture of inclusion is reinforced within our Leadership Principles, which remind team members to seek diverse perspectives, learn and be curious, and earn trust.

Work-Life Balance
We value sustainable performance. Our follow-the-sun model means you're not carrying a pager 24/7 — your node owns its shift, and clean handoffs are a core operational discipline.

Growth and Impact
This role offers a rare combination: hands-on technical security work at massive scale, leadership of a high-performing team, and direct influence over an AI-augmented security platform. You'll grow as both a security practitioner and a technical leader.

Basic qualifications

- Bachelor's degree in computer science or equivalent, or experience in IT Security
- Experience in security operations, incident response, or security engineering
- Hands-on experience investigating security incidents (malware analysis, phishing response, credential compromise, or network intrusion)
- Proficiency in Python or similar scripting language for security automation and tooling
- Experience with log analysis platforms (Splunk, ELK, or equivalent) and EDR tools (CrowdStrike, Carbon Black, or equivalent)
- Knowledge of networking protocols (HTTP, DNS, TCP/IP) and operating system internals (Windows and Linux)

Preferred qualifications

- Experience performing detection engineering in a dedicated or hybrid capacity supporting incident response and threat intelligence operations
- Experience designing or validating AI/LLM-powered automation in a security context
- Proficiency in at least one specialization domain: Malware Analysis / Reverse Engineering; Digital Forensics; Security Tool Development & Automation; Network & OS Security; Identity Management
- Experience with threat intelligence platforms and IOC enrichment (VirusTotal, MITRE ATT&CK framework)
- Experience writing detection rules (YARA, Sigma, or custom)
- Experience with Amazon Web Services and cloud security
- Track record of building security automation that measurably reduced manual operational burden
- Security certifications (GCIH, GCFA, GREM, OSCP, or equivalent) are a plus but not required

title: Senior Reliability Maintenance Engineering Technician
descriptionHtml:
Our Reliability Maintenance Engineering (RME) team is central to Amazon's commitment to innovation. As Amazon evolves and adapts, this team makes sure that the tools and technologies we use do as well. As a Senior RME Technician, you'll help us stay one step ahead, adopting the latest technologies and identifying new and efficient ways of working. In this role, you’ll pay close attention to our processes to help maintain our high standards, and you’ll put in place upgrades to take that standard even higher.

Key job responsibilities
- Demonstrate best practice on using equipment safely and monitor teams to ensure everyone follows the correct processes
- Keep track of equipment performance through visual checks, condition-based monitoring, and preventative maintenance tasks and schedule additional servicing when required
- Supervise technicians on shift to support their development and act as the first point of contact for Reliability Maintenance Engineers
- Solve issues in equipment to reduce downtime for operations so they can process packages as quickly as possible
- Support in finding ways to continually improve systems and standardise processes across the EU network

A day in the life
In every shift, you’ll be leading a team to make sure everyone has the equipment they need and that it’s running properly. That involves monitoring processes so that regulations and policies are followed and ensuring that preventative maintenance is carried out to increase equipment uptime.

With everything you observe on your shifts, you’ll suggest improvements to make our systems more efficient and productive and then implement those improvements across an EU-wide function. You’ll also be monitoring processes with tools like Scada to guarantee their performance, as well as working closely with your line manager to assist with admin tasks.

This role is located at one of our operational sites. You’ll work shift patterns, which may include some weekends and nights. As you develop your experience within this exciting part of Amazon, you’ll be well-placed to progress into more senior roles.

About the team
Our Reliability Maintenance Engineering or RME team keep our equipment performing at its best. We're a technically minded team, made up of excellent team players and guided by experienced leaders. We work together to maintain, troubleshoot and repair equipment across our global network of fulfilment centres. Some of our people are leaders, who oversee the team as they work on exciting technology – some of which only exists at Amazon.

From installing automated packaging systems to overseeing the general maintenance of a site to repairing key distribution equipment, our team handles most aspects of Amazon’s technical side. This includes keeping buildings legally compliant, so everyone is safe, and our sites are operating at maximum efficiency. There are lots of opportunities for progression, both within the RME team and more widely across Amazon.

Everything we do focuses on reducing downtime in Amazon’s crucial operations sites, so customers get their orders on time. We often work during early or late hours to carry out maintenance with minimal disruption, including night shifts. If we spot a better way to do something, we have the skills and the opportunity to develop and introduce completely new processes or cutting-edge tech like Amazon Robotics and our Complex Item Sorter.

Basic qualifications

- NVQ Level 3 in Mechanical, Electrical or Mechatronics, or completed a 4-year UK certified apprenticeship
- Work a flexible schedule/shift/work area, including weekends, nights, and/or holidays
- Experience in automated conveyors systems and controls, electrical and electronic principles, preventative maintenance procedures, blueprint and schematic reading, industrial electrical, industrial controls, industrial electronics, Programmable Logic Control (PLC) programs, National Electrical Code (NEC), work order management

Preferred qualifications

- Associate's degree in Mechatronics or a related technical field
- Experience in vendor management
- Experience with robotic maintenance
- Experience leading engineering teams as a mentor or tech lead
- Experience working with material handling equipment (MHE) safety standards in accordance with OEM requirements

title: Software Development Engineer II
descriptionHtml:
Most cloud engineers never see the physical world their software touches. On this team, you will. We build the networking that carries AWS out of the cloud and into customers' own data centers—so a hospital, a factory, or a bank can run AWS right next to the systems and data that can't leave the building. When you ship here, your code is soon routing real production traffic on real hardware in the field, all over the world.

In this role you'll design and build the services that keep that traffic flowing, and you'll own them all the way through—not just writing the code, but operating it, watching how it behaves in production, and making it more reliable over time. You'll dig into genuinely hard problems in distributed systems and networking, where the failure modes are interesting and the impact of a fix is immediate and visible.

You'll also help us work smarter, not just harder: a real part of the job is building AI agents and automation that take the repetitive engineering and operational work off the team's plate, so everyone can spend more time on the problems that actually need human judgment. If you like owning things end to end, want your work to matter in the physical world, and enjoy making a team faster as you go, you'll fit right in.

Key job responsibilities
- Design, build, test, and operate scalable, highly available control plane, distribution, and data plane services that route production traffic for AWS Outposts deployments worldwide.
- Own significant components end to end—from design documents and implementation through deployment, monitoring, and long-term operational health.
- Take ambiguous, loosely defined problems and drive them to well-reasoned technical designs, making sound tradeoffs with limited guidance.
- Write, update, and improve AI agents and automation that increase software-development and operational efficiency—reducing manual toil so the team can focus on high-judgment work.
- Raise the operational bar: improve observability, harden deployment pipelines, and drive down the time-to-detect and time-to-mitigate for the systems you own.
- Participate in an on-call rotation for the services you own, and lead the investigation and resolution of production issues, including root-cause analysis and long-term corrective actions.
- Write high-quality, well-tested, maintainable code and hold a high bar in design and code reviews.
- Brainstorm ideas with teammates and review key technical decisions and designs with senior engineers and leadership to pressure-test approaches and align on direction.
- Mentor junior engineers, share context generously, and contribute to the technical direction and engineering standards of the team.
- Collaborate across teams—partner service teams (e.g., S3, EBS, Route 53), networking, and hardware/edge teams—to deliver features that span organizational boundaries.

A day in the life
Most of your day is spent designing, building, and operating the services that route traffic for AWS Outposts and Local Gateway, keeping them running reliably for customers around the world. You'll write and review code, and you'll keep an eye on your dashboards to make sure the changes you ship are flowing safely into production and everything you own is healthy.

You'll also spend real time making the team faster: building and improving AI agents and automation that take routine engineering and operational work off everyone's plate, so we can focus on the harder, more interesting problems. Ideas come from everywhere here, so expect to brainstorm with teammates, sketch out approaches together, and talk through your bigger technical decisions with experienced engineers and leaders who'll help you sharpen your thinking. You'll also work closely with partner teams like S3, EBS, and Route 53 to ship things that span more than one service.

Beyond the day-to-day, you'll have the room to dig into ambiguous problems, decide how the services you own should evolve, and help the engineers around you grow. Because our software runs in customer data centers all over the world, you'll see the real impact of your work quickly—and you'll have a genuine say in how we make it more reliable and easier to operate over time.


About the team
Our team is focused on building reliable, scalable software that customers depend on every day. We value collaboration, clear communication, and a commitment to getting the details right. We believe that great software comes from inclusive teams where every voice is heard and good ideas can come from anyone. As we look ahead, we are investing in new capabilities and technologies that will expand our impact, and you will play a key role in shaping that direction. If you are excited about solving hard problems alongside thoughtful engineers, we would love to hear from you.

Basic qualifications

- 3+ years of non-internship professional software development experience
- 2+ years of non-internship design or architecture (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems experience
- 1+ years of software development engineer or related occupational experience
- 1+ years of designing and developing large-scale, multi-tiered, multi-threaded, embedded or distributed software applications, tools, systems, and services using: C#, C++, Java, or Perl experience
- 1+ years of Object Oriented Design experience
- Bachelor's degree or foreign equivalent in Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, or a related field
- Experience programming with at least one software programming language

Preferred qualifications

- 3+ years of full software development life cycle, including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, and operations experience

title: Network Loss Program Manager, Amazon Transportation Brazil
descriptionHtml:
Are you looking for the opportunity to create substantial impact on business profitability through the reduction of operational waste across one of Amazon's fastest-growing markets? The Network Losses Program Manager role in Brazil is that opportunity.

As a Network Loss Program Manager, you will own the end-to-end strategy and execution of network loss reduction across Brazil's Fulfillment Center (FC) and Transportation networks. You will be responsible for overseeing network loss metrics, driving operational improvements, and managing product implementations that eliminate shrinkage, damages, concessions, and undeliverable losses across the entire supply chain. The scope of impact spans Transportation Losses, FC Losses (Warehouse Lost, Warehouse Damage, FC Shrinkage, Item Missing), and seller reimbursement optimization — working in close collaboration with FC/Transportation Operations, ACES, SL&P, NCRC, Products, Finance, and RoW Network Losses teams.

At Amazon, we're working to be the most customer-centric company on earth. Our team drives innovation while supporting continuous operational improvement. Brazil's network loss landscape presents a unique challenge: with several initiatives across three workstreams, a rapidly expanding warehouse footprint, and a complex reverse logistics network, this role requires someone who can connect the dots across multiple programs, drive accountability through mechanisms, and deliver measurable financial impact.

This opportunity requires excellent troubleshooting, problem solving, and the ability to succeed in a fast-paced, ambiguous, and technical environment. Ownership of work is extremely important, and candidates should have a proven record of driving operations, process fixes, and strategic initiatives to completion. The ideal candidate is motivated, data-driven, and agile — with strong cross-functional influencing skills and the ability to operate at both strategic and tactical levels.

Key job responsibilities
1. Metrics Ownership: Own and manage Brazil's Network Loss metrics including Transportation Shrinkage, Warehouse Losses, Reimbursements and DPMO across In-Facility, In-Transit, and On-Road segments. Monitor success metrics on a daily/weekly basis through WBRs and MBRs. Deep dive operational data to identify root causes for losses across the network.

2. Product & Process Implementation: Drive product implementation in operations (e.g., URL compliance, TEP expansion, recovery mechanisms, repacking programs, reverse network design) and operational process solutions to eliminate losses. Partner with RoW Products to adapt global solutions to Brazil's context. Manage and expand loss recovery programs including 3P carrier. Track financial impact and drive accountability.

3. Cross-Functional Collaboration: Work with FC Operations, Transportation, Continuous Improvement, Quality, Loss Prevention, Finance to build visibility on loss themes, set up mitigation plans.

4. Reverse Logistics & ReLo Center: Support the design and operationalization of Brazil's Reverse Logistics (ReLo) Center, driving improvements in undeliverable grading, sellable yield, and recommerce recovery rates.

5. Standardization & Governance: Improve operational processes by standardizing metrics, SOPs, and governance mechanisms across Brazil's FC and transportation network.

6. Stakeholder Communication: Communicate results, risks, and strategic recommendations to senior leadership through structured mechanisms including WBRs, MBRs, and STL syncs.

Basic qualifications

- Experience using data and metrics to determine and drive improvements
- Experience owning program strategy, end to end delivery, and communicating results to senior leadership
- Experience in program or project management
- Experience in supply chain

Preferred qualifications

- Master's degree, or MBA in business, operations, human resources, adult education, organizational development, instructional design or related field
- Experience leading process improvements

title: Operations Manager, UKIE AMZL, AMZL
descriptionHtml:
Operations is the beating heart of Amazon. This key part of our business makes sure we fulfil and dispatch orders efficiently so that our customers get their items on time. It’s driven by Operations Managers who bring the team together to push excellence in safety, quality and productivity across our sites. At your site, you’ll lead other managers and create the operational plan that helps your teams meet their targets. This role is all about driving operational excellence to create the Amazon of tomorrow.

Key job responsibilities
- Manage and develop a team of Area Managers
- Lead operational teams on a shift, deal with issues, and positively impact site performance
- Analyse shift performance against relevant business objectives, and put in place actions to improve our operational excellence
- Work closely with other support teams, including HR, Finance, Health and Safety, and Security
- Design and deliver initiatives across the sites to improve operational performance

A day in the life
You’ll lead shifts at one of our operational sites. You’ll also be the key link between a number of teams, including finance, safety and operations integration teams. That means you’ll be close to the day-to-day operations at your site but also contribute to new ways to innovate at your site.

A typical day will involve meetings with different areas of the business, deep diving into performance and risk metrics for sites, and looking ahead to prepare for different levels of demand. Every day will also involve mentoring and coaching your team. You’ll be a source of leadership and support your team to be the best managers they can be.



About the team
About the team
Amazon Logistics, or AMZL, handles ‘last mile’ delivery duties in partnership with third-party distribution businesses. We utilise creative thinking and continuous improvement initiatives to get millions of physical products into the hands of our customers. Our goal is to make our customers’ delivery experience as smooth as possible and roll out global delivery solutions for our newest concepts, like Amazon Fresh, Prime Now and Amazon Restaurants.

There are two sides to what we do. Our ‘under the roof’ associates process millions of products for dispatch to our delivery teams. Our team is people-focused and supportive, particularly as lots of our people work through the night. We focus mostly on operations, with 24/7 shifts in most of our locations.

Meanwhile, our ‘on the road’ people work with Amazon Flex - a network of delivery contractors. Every year, we continually raise the bar for customer experience with new, innovative delivery services. We look for new ways to overcome industry wide logistics challenges and new ideas to reduce our carbon footprint, supported by a portfolio of vehicles (including Electric Vehicles) and technology to help us do just that.

Basic qualifications

- Bachelor's degree, or Master's degree
- Experience within a distribution center, logistics, or manufacturing environment
- Experience working with multiple groups of stakeholders
- Advanced proficiency in verbal and written English and upper intermediate proficiency in the local language

- Preferred qualifications are not required to apply for a position at Amazon. If you have all the basic qualifications above, we’d love to hear from you.
- A bachelor’s, advanced or master’s degree in engineering, supply chain, logistics, or manufacturing
- Experience in managing third-party relationships
- Experience of applying Lean, Six Sigma, and Kaizen methodologies

title: Area Manager II, YOW3
descriptionHtml:
Our WW Operations network delivers millions of packages and smiles to Amazon customers every day. We are looking for motivated, customer-focused individuals who want to join our team as an Area Manager. In this role, you will lead a team of hourly workforce and will be responsible for engaging your team during their shifts to maintain the highest levels of safety, quality, attendance, and performance. You will also play a key role in maintaining our customer expectations to ensure customer orders are delivered at the right time, to the right location.

Our Operation’s workflow has three major components: First mile - where the product is housed and ready for order; Middle mile - where the order is hauled to your area; and Last mile - when the product is delivered to the customer’s door. Please note that all workflows have slight building variations, but one thing is constant: our vision and dedication to the customer.

Our fulfillment network launches new Operations sites every year, providing various opportunities for your professional growth. We hire Area Managers based on location preference and the business’ current openings.

Key job responsibilities
- Support, mentor, and motivate your hourly workforce
- Manage safety, quality, productivity, and customer delivery promises
- Collaborate with all support teams including Safety, Engineering, Loss Prevention, Quality Assurance, Human Resources to develop plans to meet business objectives
- Lift up to 49 pounds and frequently push, pull, squat, bend, and reach
- Stand/walk for up to 12 hours during shifts
- Work in an environment where the noise level varies and can be loud
- Work in an environment that is subject to variable temperatures and weather (delivery stations include outside loading departments)
- Continuously climb and descend stairs (applies to sites with stairs)

A day in the life
As an Area Manager II at an Amazon fulfillment center, you'll act as a strategic leader overseeing upto 80 associates while driving department level operational improvements. You'll conduct planning sessions with your team, coaching them through operational challenges while developing their leadership capabilities. On a typical day, you'll partner cross-functionally with teams such as Quality, HR, and Safety to implement scalable process improvements that could impact 200+ associates across multiple workflows. You'll diagnose root causes of performance gaps using advanced analytics, facilitate alignment meetings with senior leadership on department-level goals, and make data-driven decisions that balance competing priorities. You would leverage your strategic thinking to review department-wide metrics, and plan initiatives that directly impact millions of customer orders while maintaining high levels of engagement, safety, quality, and productivity standards.

Basic qualifications

- 2+ years of employee and performance management experience
- Bachelor's degree or equivalent, or 2+ years of Amazon (blue badge/FTE) experience
- Work a flexible schedule/shift/work area, including weekends, nights, and/or holidays

Preferred qualifications

- 1+ years of performance metrics, process improvement or lean techniques experience
- Experience that includes strong analytical skills, attention to detail, and effective communication abilities, or experience working with customers with a passion for delivering exceptional service
- Experience in the management of large teams (50+ members)
- Experience with process improvement techniques such as Kaizen, Lean Manufacturing or Six Sigma
- Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Operations, Supply Chain/Logistics, or a related field
- Experience in one or more of the following industries: shipping/logistics distribution centers, manufacturing environments, hospitality, healthcare, retail, and customer-facing / customer-service environments

title: 2027 Applied Scientist Internship – PhD, Amazon University Talent Acquisition
descriptionHtml:
We're building systems that turn research into real-world impact — developing AI-driven detection systems that identify and remediate security access violations across Amazon's global operations, and building ML solutions that leverage product images, text, and tabular data to improve safety and compliance mechanisms across Amazon's entire product catalog. If this sounds interesting to you then we have a range of opportunities for you to explore.

We're looking for PhD students across multiple research domains to invent, design, and implement state-of-the-art solutions for never-before-solved problems. Your work here won't just stay in a notebook — it ships to production and reaches customers worldwide.

Check out the details below including the job responsibilities, team details, and basic qualifications before submitting your application.

Key job responsibilities
As an Applied Science Intern, you will own the design and development of end-to-end systems. You'll have the opportunity to write technical white papers, create roadmaps and drive production level projects that will support Amazon Science.

You will work closely with Amazon scientists and other science interns to develop solutions and deploy them into production. You will have the opportunity to design new algorithms, models, or other technical solutions whilst experiencing Amazon's customer focused culture.

The ideal intern should have the ability to work with diverse groups of people and cross-functional teams to solve complex business problems.


A day in the life
You'll spend your first weeks scoping your project with your mentor, then own the research and implementation end-to-end.

Your work could involve building graph-based ML models and knowledge graphs that detect and remediate access violations at global scale, developing behavioral pattern clustering and automated reasoning systems for security operations, or researching multimodal and computer vision approaches on product catalog data to improve safety and compliance mechanisms — depending on the team you're matched with.

Many interns publish at top-tier conferences or see their work deployed to production before the internship ends. Interns may also be considered for a return offer at the end of their internship, subject to performance evaluation and headcount availability.

Further benefits of an Amazon Science internship include;

- All of our internships offer a competitive salary
- Interns are paired with an experienced manager and mentor(s)
- Interns get invited to different intern program or office events
- Interns can build their professional and personal network with other Amazon Scientists
- Interns can potentially publish work at top tier conferences

About the team
We generally hire interns for multiple teams in Romania, including but not limited to;

• CoSS — Research and develop ML solutions that improve safety and compliance across Amazon's entire product catalog working with tabular, textual, and product image data using deep learning, computer vision, LLMs, and multimodal models

• Monitored Access Detection — Build AI-driven detection and remediation systems that identify global access violations across Amazon — leveraging knowledge graphs, graph modeling, behavioral pattern clustering, generative AI, and reinforcement learning to create a self-improving, closed-loop security system.

You'll submit a single application and we'll match you with science teams best aligned with your research interests.

Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis, and your application stays active until we find a team match or confirm there are no matches available.

Start dates are available throughout the year for durations of between 3–6 months. Please note, each team has different start date and duration preferences — your recruiter will confirm the preferences of the team you're matched with prior to interviewing.

We offer science internships in multiple locations across the EMEA region and you can indicate your interest in all these locations by applying here (Austria, Estonia, France, Germany, Ireland, Israel, Italy, Jordan, Luxembourg, Netherlands, Poland, Romania, South Africa, Spain, Sweden, UAE, and UK).

Please note we do not offer remote internships.

- Are enrolled in a PhD in computer science, machine learning, engineering, or related fields
- Experience programming in Java, C++, Python or related language
- Speak, write, and read fluently in English

Preferred qualifications

- Have publications at top-tier peer-reviewed conferences or journals
- Experience in solving business problems through machine learning, data mining and statistical algorithms
- Experience in designing experiments and statistical analysis of results

descriptionHtml:
Application deadline: Nov 10, 2026

Amazon Web Services (AWS) is proud to be the pioneer and recognized leader in Cloud Computing. Our web services provide IT infrastructure used by hundreds of thousands of developers and businesses worldwide, from startups to Global 500 companies across all industries.

AWS is looking for an experienced Storage Solutions Architect to serve as a Subject Matter Expert (SME) for AWS DataSync, AWS Transfer Family, and AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery (DRS). You will be a technical authority working closely with service teams to drive innovation and adoption while supporting field teams and strategic customers across enterprise migrations, data center exits, managed file transfer (MFT) modernization, and disaster recovery.

The ideal candidate is equally comfortable diving deep into storage service internals with engineering teams and explaining complex architectures to technical decision-makers. You will partner with AWS storage service teams to influence roadmaps, document best practices, and drive feature adoption through technical content creation and industry event presentations.

In this role, you will partner with Storage Product and GTM teams to enable key technical use cases and drive service adoption. A key focus is translating complex storage and data-movement requirements into scalable, resilient architectures and supporting the field through large-scale data center migrations, modernizing managed file transfer workflows, and designing recovery strategies that keep critical workloads resilient. Through thought leadership, you will establish best practices, propose service enhancements, and create technical content that enables successful implementation of AWS storage solutions.

This role combines service expertise with strategic customer engagement. Travel requirements are approximately 25%, primarily for speaking engagements and technical events.

Key job responsibilities

- Capture and advocate for customer feedback to influence the DataSync, Transfer Family, and DRS roadmaps, including driving resolution of critical feature gaps blocking large migration and recovery pipelines

You will ideate, create, design, and drive completion of deliverables that structurally improve the connection between upstream operations and delivery outcomes.

Key job responsibilities
- Define and maintain the metrics framework that connects upstream process performance to NA Grocery delivery outcomes.

title: Principal Program Manager, WHS Strategy, Workplace Health and Safety
descriptionHtml:
Amazon's Workplace Health and Safety (WHS) organization is responsible for safeguarding the health and wellbeing of more than 1.2 million operations employees across Amazon's global operations network. WHS advances safety performance through three pillars: people, programs, and technology. The organization builds a self-sustaining safety culture, prevents incidents through engineering and standardized operational practices, and applies artificial intelligence and computer vision to drive faster, proactive safety interventions at scale.

We are seeking a Principal Program Manager to lead the WHS Strategy team. This is a high-visibility leadership role at the intersection of enterprise strategy, executive communications, and operational safety performance. The leader in this position will serve as the primary owner of WHS's strategic planning cycle and will be accountable for the quality, coherence, and timeliness of the safety narrative presented to Amazon's most senior executives, including VP, SVP, and Board-level audiences.

This role requires a strategic leader who is effective under pressure, comfortable navigating organizational complexity, and capable of exercising sound judgment on matters with broad impact. The right candidate brings deep experience partnering directly with executive leadership, the ability to bring structure to ambiguous problems, and a consistent track record of delivering on high-stakes commitments. A core requirement is the ability to take complex, technical safety programs and communicate them with clarity and simplicity to audiences ranging from front-line operators to Board members. Exceptional written and verbal communication skills are not a differentiator for this role; they are a baseline requirement.

Key job responsibilities
This leader will own the end-to-end strategic planning lifecycle for WHS, including the development of 1 to 3 year strategic roadmaps, annual operating plans (OP1/OP2), and recurring executive reviews at monthly, quarterly, and annual cadences. Specific accountabilities include:

Collecting, synthesizing, and integrating strategic inputs from WHS teams across the organization, then drafting that content into a single, unified voice that reflects the WHS leader's perspective, ensuring consistent messaging, tone, and narrative alignment from document to document.

Authoring and managing the portfolio of WHS executive-level documents, ensuring analytical rigor, narrative precision, and strategic alignment across every deliverable that represents WHS to senior leadership.

Partnering with operations, engineering, and technology organizations across Amazon to integrate health and safety priorities into their strategic plans, influencing outcomes without direct authority.

Designing and governing the mechanisms through which safety data is reported to leadership, including ownership of data lock processes that ensure consistency and accuracy across all executive-facing materials.

Identifying opportunities to modernize how safety performance data is visualized, shared, and consumed by decision-makers at every level, raising the standard for insight-driven reporting.

Managing the enterprise planning calendar and orchestrating cross-functional inputs from a broad coalition of WHS field teams, central program teams, and operations stakeholders globally.

Translating complex operational programs, technical initiatives, and nuanced safety concepts into clear, concise, and accessible content for executive and non-specialist audiences.

A day in the life
You are a results-oriented leader with a genuine intellectual curiosity about what drives safety performance in complex operational environments. You combine strategic thinking with operational discipline: you can frame a multi-year vision and then build the mechanisms to bring it to life. You are comfortable being the person in the room who is expected to have the answer, and you hold yourself to that standard.

You bring a data-driven approach to every decision, an instinct for continuous improvement, and the organizational fluency to move work forward across teams that do not report to you. You are energized by ambiguity, not paralyzed by it. You communicate with clarity and economy, recognizing that at the executive level, every word carries weight. You are ready to own the strategic direction of safety for one of the world's largest employers and to ensure that direction is understood, aligned, and acted upon from the front line to the boardroom.
This is an in-office role requiring five days per week on-site. Travel is expected at 10 to 20 percent annually.

About the team
The WHS Strategy team functions as the connective tissue between WHS's technical and operational organizations and Amazon's executive leadership. The team builds and manages the mechanisms through which WHS compiles, creates, and refines the strategic planning and reporting documents that represent safety performance at the highest levels of the company. This is the program management group that owns the majority of WHS executive-level content and serves as the central authority for safety data and narrative consistency across Amazon.

The team operates as a trusted, high-credibility point of contact for a large global network of senior and executive stakeholders. The work is inherently cross-functional, requiring the ability to synthesize competing inputs, reconcile inconsistencies in data or direction, and produce a unified strategic view under tight timelines. The team's output directly shapes how Amazon's senior leaders understand and act on safety.

Basic qualifications

- 5+ years of cross functional project delivery experience
- 5+ years of program or project management experience
- 7+ years of working cross functionally with tech and non-tech teams experience
- Experience using data and metrics to drive improvements
- Experience in written and verbal communication skills to communicate with technical and non-technical audiences, including senior leadership
- Bachelor's Degree in Occupational Safety, Environmental Sciences, Engineering, Communications, Supply Chain or related field of study.

Preferred qualifications

- MBA
- Experience defining and executing program requirements
- Experience managing, analyzing and communicating results to senior leadership
- 6+ years of increasing responsibilities in EHS or environmental programs in manufacturing, production, or service operations experience, or Bachelor's degree

title: Sr. Electrical Engineer, Sustainability Engineering
descriptionHtml:
The Sustainability Engineering team is seeking a Senior Electrical Engineer to drive the definition, development, and continuous improvement of electrical infrastructure standards across Amazon facilities in Europe.

You will join a team which:
• Enables EV charging infrastructure implementation through electrical design definition and review
• Develops grid infrastructure standards spanning high-voltage up to 24 kV (HV) and low-voltage (LV) systems, ensuring a coordinated and resilient approach to grid design
• Explores emerging technologies to address evolving sustainability needs, with emphasis on smart grid integration, efficiency, and resilience
• Drives end-to-end deployment of EV chargers and other sustainability technologies across European sites
• Defines processes for procurement and maintenance of electrical and sustainability infrastructure
• Owns cost budgeting, forecasting, and tracking across sustainability programmes

Possible locations for this role: Luxembourg, London, Munich, Milan, Madrid, and Barcelona

Amazon is committed to building a sustainable future for our customers, local communities, and the planet. Under The Climate Pledge, we committed to achieving net-zero carbon across our business by 2040, ten years ahead of the Paris Agreement. To get there, we need driven people who are dedicated to making a meaningful impact through sustainable energy technologies and scalable infrastructure design.

Key job responsibilities
• Own and develop electrical equipment standards, including standard designs for core electrical infrastructure in partnership with manufacturers and internal stakeholders
• Perform design validation and review to ensure compliance with established electrical standards during installation and commissioning of infrastructure
• Act as subject matter expert (SME) for LV and HV (up to 24kV) electrical systems
• Align stakeholder expectations and define technical requirements for EV charging network infrastructure and smart grid deployments
• Drive the technology roadmap for electrical infrastructure, including EV chargers, substations, energy efficiency solutions, and IoT technologies (e.g. smart metres)
• Develop business cases and present recommendations to leadership to secure approval for programme scoping and investment decisions
• Coordinate with programme managers to ensure quality and standards compliance across large-scale installations
• Drive process improvement across commissioning, audit, value engineering, and cost control activities


A day in the life
Your day could include engagement with all levels of the organisation and multiple stakeholder groups to drive short-, mid-, and long-term technical decisions with large-scale impact across the Amazon network. You will also work with partners from Operations, Reliability & Maintenance, Health and Safety, Global Fleet Product, Finance, Procurement, and external vendors to design and deploy electrical infrastructure across Amazon’s operational sites in Europe.

About the team
The Sustainability Engineering team drives the execution and deployment of EV charging infrastructure, grid connections, and smart grid solutions across Amazon’s European sites. We manage supply chain, procurement, and maintenance activities, and define the processes that ensure consistent, scalable delivery. To enable this, the team develops and continuously improves electrical standards and technologies that underpin reliable, compliant deployment at pace. We power Amazon’s sustainable growth through operational excellence and continuous innovation.

Basic qualifications

- Master’s degree or Ph.D. in Electrical Engineering or a closely related field, with experience in electrical infrastructure design, standards development, or large-scale electrical systems implementation
- Experience driving technical programmes across multiple European countries in a corporate environment
- Demonstrated knowledge of HV and/or LV electrical distribution systems (up to 24kV) and applicable standards

Preferred qualifications

- Experience in technical program and product management, technical development or related roles in the industrial EV charging solutions sector
- Proficiency in one or more European languages (in addition to English)
- Experience working with public grid operators or Distribution System Operators (DSOs)
- Working knowledge of national grid codes and DSO requirements in one or more EU/UK markets
- Experience with protection coordination, fault level analysis, or power systems modelling
- Chartered Electrical Engineer (CEng) or equivalent professional registration

title: Snr Process Improvement Specialist, Planning & Reporting, EU Ops Sustainability, EU Ops Sustainability
descriptionHtml:
EU Operations Sustainability drives the decarbonization of Amazon's operational footprint across Europe, focusing on reducing environmental impact from transportation, buildings, and energy consumption. The team develops and executes strategies spanning First Mile, Middle Mile, and Last Mile logistics — including energy efficiency, renewable energy, building material decarbonization and climate resiliency and adaptation, at fulfillment centers, sort centres and delivery stations. Working cross-functionally with EU Operations, WW Sustainability, engineering and procurement, the EU Ops Sustainability team translates Amazon's Climate Pledge commitments into actionable programs with measurable targets. The team navigates also the evolving European regulatory landscape to ensure compliance while identifying opportunities to accelerate decarbonization ahead of mandated timelines.

EU Ops Sustainability is looking for an analytical, detail-oriented, and self-directed Senior Process Improvement Specialist to own all planning and reporting activities that track carbon, energy, and beyond-carbon plans on behalf of the entire EU Ops Sustainability organization. This is the single-threaded planning and reporting owner for the EU Ops Sustainability team: you will build and run the mechanisms that turn complex sustainability data across First Mile, Middle Mile, and Last Mile into a reliable, auditable single source of truth that leaders use to make decisions.
This role supports our Climate Pledge goal of net zero carbon by 2040 by establishing rigorous, repeatable planning cycles and reporting mechanisms across carbon abatement, carbon intensity, energy, and beyond-carbon programs (e.g., waste, water, and circularity). To be successful, you need a passion for sustainability and data, the ability to process large and imperfect datasets to drive business decisions, and the judgment to know which numbers matter. The successful candidate must have strong analytical skills, familiarity with ETL and SQL, and the ability to apply systems thinking to complex, fast-moving problems.
You must be comfortable working independently in an ambiguous, high-pressure environment, identifying sources of uncertainty, and finding data to fill the gaps where needed. You are not only able to develop and drive high-level planning strategy, but can also roll up your sleeves, dig in, and get the job done—consolidating inputs from stakeholders across business units, resolving data-quality issues, and communicating results clearly to all levels of leadership.

Key job responsibilities
This role is inherently cross-functional - responsibilities include (but are not limited to):
• Own the EU Ops Sustainability planning calendar end to end—coordinate and deliver the annual and multi-year planning cycles (OP1/3YF, OP2, and Glidepath) for carbon, energy, and beyond-carbon plans, gathering and reconciling inputs from stakeholders across all business units.
• Build, maintain, and continuously improve the carbon, energy, and beyond-carbon reporting suite— co-developing reports, dashboards, and metrics that distill complex data into actionable insights and inform strategy across First Mile, Middle Mile, and Last Mile, working with the Sustainability Data and Analytics team within EU Ops Sustainability.
• Serve as the single source of truth for EU Ops Sustainability planning and actuals, owning the data structures, definitions, and methodology that underpin regional reporting.
• Run the sustainability month-end close for the region—ensuring data quality, timely resolution of data issues, and alignment of carbon abatement and carbon intensity reporting on a monthly basis.
• Develop and implement key performance indicators (KPIs) for the portfolio of sustainability programs, providing visibility into milestones and performance across projects.
• Establish the operating rhythm—lead programmatic reviews (MBR/QBR) and prepare variance commentary and metrics for leadership reporting, communicating status, risks, and course-correction strategies to senior leadership.

About the team
EU Ops Sustainability’s vision is to accelerate decarbonization across First Mile, Middle Mile, and Last Mile to ensure we achieve Net Zero Carbon by 2040. To drive this change, we integrate sustainability into decision-making for Amazon’s operations and supply chain. The EU strategy is aligned with the guidance provided by the WW Operations Sustainability team, and this role is central to making that strategy measurable and accountable.
We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why flexible work hours and arrangements are part of our culture.

Basic qualifications

- Bachelor's degree in econometrics, statistics, industrial engineering, operations research, optimization, data mining, analytics, or equivalent quantitative field
- Experience in program or project management
- Experience using data and metrics to determine and drive improvements
- Experience owning program strategy, end-to-end delivery, and communicating results to senior leadership
- Knowledge of Excel at an intermediate level (e.g., pivot tables & charts, multiple criteria lookups, nested logical/IF formulas, data cleansing, array formulas, etc.)
- Experience working with data analytics and using these metrics to identify problems, or experience in an operational role
- Experience managing multiple competing priorities simultaneously and driving goals to completion

Preferred qualifications

- Bachelor's degree, or Master's degree in supply chain, business, engineering, finance or related technical or quantitative field
- Experience developing and implementing of standards, policies and programs or equivalent
- Knowledge of at least one data-focused technology tool, such as Python, SQL, Alteryx, Amazon QuickSight, or similar
- Experience in analysing data and creating reports for leadership
- Experience in logistics, transportation, supply chain, import/export operations, or data entry/data administration
- Great attention to detail, strong financial acumen, and excellent written and verbal communication.

title: Responsable contrôle d'inventaire et qualité (H/F)
descriptionHtml:
Do you aim to have a dynamic impact on the world? Are you up for creating solutions and solving tomorrow’s problems today? Then we have the opportunity for you! We are looking to hire an ICQA Area Manager to be part of our fulfillment center Inventory Control and Quality Assurance (ICQA) team. Our fulfillment centers (FC) sit at the heart of Amazon’s rapidly growing operations network: they are where we manage our fast-moving inventory. In each fulfillment center, our teams stow deliveries, pick products, package them up and ship them out; each of these groups have played their part in taking us where we are today. These fulfillment centers are fast-paced and high reward environments, where adherence to policies and procedures is key. We need a leader that ensures we deliver as reliably as ever to our customers, while making sure our teams deliver on customer obsession.

Key job responsibilities
Lead and supervise a team of hourly Associates (including Team Leads and Data Analyst) assigned to inventory control, quality assurance and problem solve operations within the fulfillment center
Support safety programs and compliance to ensure a safe work environment for all associates. Work with Operations and other Support teams to establish, influence and adhere to policies and procedures
Coordinate inventory control, quality assurance and problem solve operations in accordance to network strategies and ensuring compliance and consistency with SOX
Conduct shift planning and forecasting, alongside assigning and directing work. Oversee projects to streamline processes, increase quality and optimize productivity
Ensure KPIs are reviewed on a daily, weekly, or monthly basis and perform quality analysis on any behaviors/processes that could impact inventory integrity and Customer esperience
Gain expertise in key fulfillment center process paths and its exceptions handling in order to drive processes continuous improvement alongside the operations management team
Support in interviewing and training fulfillment center managers and associates, developing talent and hiring the next generation of managers

A day in the life
You'll work shifts at one of our fulfillment centers, overseeing inventory control, quality assurance and problem solve operations. Your day typically starts with a team huddle, where you'll review previous shift performance, set daily goals, and address any ongoing issues.Throughout your shift, you will conduct inventory discrepancies analysis, oversee the resolution of receiving issues, and coach team members on accuracy improvement.You'll regularly analyze data, looking for trends and opportunities for process improvement, collaborating with other partners in FC operations or in central teams that own Catalogue, Procurement, Supply Chain, Process Engineering, Loss Prevention and Program Management. You'll need to make quick, informed decisions to keep operations running smoothly.Throughout your shift, you'll be on the floor, observing processes, coaching team members, and ensuring safety standards are maintained in you area. You'll also dedicate time to developing your team members, providing feedback, and identifying training needs. By shift end, you'll prepare a handover for the next shift, summarizing key events, ongoing issues, and priorities. You'll leave knowing you've contributed to maintaining inventory accuracy, resolving inbound challenges, and ultimately ensuring customer satisfaction through efficient and accurate fulfillment operations.

About the team
The EU ICQA mission is to prevent and remove customer-facing defects with the goal to provide a world class service to our customers, at the lowest possible cost. The Vision of ICQA is to exceed customers’ expectations, both buyers and sellers. We drive defect-free order fulfillment by operating in the most efficient and accurate way through the creation and implementation of quality standards in our FC processes (receive, stow, count, pick, pack & ship) up to our sellers and customers. We lead with empathy to create a safer, more productive, higher performing and more diverse work environment. We commit to empower and support our team members to grow and achieve their aspirations.

Basic qualifications

- A degree from an accredited university or equivalent experience in operations management Relevant experience in performing data analysis and understanding data sets and tools Proficient in the local language and English, both spoken and written Advanced MS Office suite user, especially Excel

Preferred qualifications

- Preferred qualifications are not required to apply for a position at Amazon. If you have all the basic qualifications above, we'd love to hear from you. A resilient, focused problem solver and self-starter, with the ability to multi-task and prioritize in a complex and ambiguous environment Strong commitment to employee development, as well as an exceptional level of dedication, motivation to team management Proven ability to influence peers or stakeholders, with varying levels of seniority, within Ops organization A focused problem-solver and self-starter, with the ability to multi-task and prioritize in a complex environment Knowledge of and experience with Lean and Six Sigma methodologies and techniques

Amazon est un employeur engagé pour l'égalité des chances. Nous sommes convaincus qu'une main d'oeuvre diversifée est essentielle à notre réussite. Nous prenons nos décisions de recrutement en fonction de votre expérience et de vos compétences. Nous apprécions votre envie de découvrir, d'inventer, de simplifier et de construire. La protection de votre vie privée et la sécurité de vos données constituent depuis longtemps une priorité absolue pour Amazon. Veuillez consulter notre Politique de Confidentialité pour en savoir plus sur la façon dont nous collectons, utilisons et traitons les données personnelles de nos candidats.

title: Sr. Analyst, Last Mile volume, EU LTP Last Mile Analytics
descriptionHtml:
[This role can be based in Luxembourg, Madrid Barcelona, Paris, Milan]

It’s always Day One at Amazon, and today is no different for our last-mile transportation network. We view transportation as a critical element in delivering on our promise to customers, from the moment they click “Buy” on Amazon to the time their package arrives at their doorstep. Optimizing the last-mile network — designing the number, size, and locations of delivery stations, as well as the jurisdiction of each delivery station — enables our portfolio of innovative, fast, and reliable delivery services for customers across Europe.

The EU Long-Term Planning Last Mile Analytics team owns and produces the strategic plan across a planning horizon ranging from 13 weeks to 5+ years for EU Amazon Logistics, and provides insights and recommendations to support key decisions. We generate business insights for the EU leadership team to make strategic decisions by surfacing the risks and opportunities associated with each plan we produce, detailing why and how plans vary, and providing scenario analyses related to the Last Mile Delivery Station network, volume, and productivity.

We are looking for an experienced Sr. Analyst to join the EU LTP Last Mile Analytics team. As a Sr. Analyst, you will develop multi-year operating plans for delivery stations and work with the DS Topology, S&OP, and Labor Planning teams to track the progress of multi-year plans, build feedback mechanisms to improve planning, and develop new processes.

You will lead continuous improvement projects for our planning process, as well as build and prioritize feature requirements for the further development of advanced optimization, forecasting, and tracking capabilities for multi-million-dollar programs aimed at solving business problems in the transportation domain. Your role is highly visible, as you will be in regular communication with senior Operations leaders, up to VP and Director level, within STEP (Transportation Supply Chain).

Supply chain or business planning experience, cross-team coordination, project management, executive presentation skills, and a proven track record of delivering results are essential. Finally, you will own the documentation and presentation of network plans, risks, and contingencies to all levels of Operations leadership on a regular basis.

Ready for the challenge?

About the team

Basic qualifications

- Bachelor's degree or above in engineering, project management, operations, logistics, supply chain or related field
- Experience handling multiple competing priorities and complex projects with multiple stakeholders (e.g. definition of accurate network expansion plans, vendor development, quality assurance, design and cost improvement, team and stakeholder engagement)
- Speak, write, and read fluently in English
- Experience prior success in driving execution of large-scale project plans with multiple teams in support of business goals
- Experience delivering results for large, cross-functional initiatives/projects, or experience in building financial and operational reports/data sets that inform business decision-making
- Experience managing challenging assignments with aggressive schedules
- Experience demonstrating strong analytical abilities and confidence in the use of data
- Experience in strategic planning
- Experience communicating clearly and concisely with leadership, stakeholders, and cross-functional teams

Preferred qualifications

- Experience in transportation or supply chain

title: Data Center Capacity Planning TIPM, Capacity Delivery Planning
descriptionHtml:
Work hard, have fun, and make history at Amazon Web Services!

The AWS Infrastructure Capacity Planning Team is searching for a passionate and talented Regional Capacity Planner to drive capacity planning across multiple AWS regions, resulting in a single plan of record for each region. You will have goals to improve infrastructure utilization as well as availability. You will work across the AWS Organization to align demand with data center capacity and coordinate execution planning across AWS.

If you love being at the forefront of industry growth and development, applying your people skills and your analytical skills to drive insight into the business and improve the quality of key inputs, then this is a spot for you. This is a high impact role offering an opportunity work cross-functionally on lasting solutions that impact the long-term future of AWS.

Key job responsibilities
• Plan data center capacity for the 0-24-month horizon.
• Plan for rack retirements and migrations based on infra needs.
• Plan for network requirements per site for order plan and network reserve.
• Plan and initiate dedicated spine builds, intercept builds and resize per the recommended planning values.
• Intercept builds for emerging customer requirements and communicate changes per established process.
• Resolve racks on hold blockers to meet the org goals.
• Resolve blocked order blockers to meet the org goals.
• Resolve position usability defects to meet the org goals.
• Initiate and manage projects to meet power usage targets.
• Perform customer impact analysis as needed.
• Work with supply chain and service owners to prioritize rack landings in constrained regions.
• Prepare and present mitigated views in weekly review meetings.
• Deep dive and communicate supply changes (WoW, MoM).
• Perform position inventory and build updates as needed.
• Work with brick planners and network TPMs on resolving position constraints.

About the team
AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

Basic qualifications

- 3+ years of technical infrastructure management experience
- Knowledge of best practices and emerging technologies, related to infrastructure (i.e. network, data center, hardware, software)
- Experience with varying scenarios of infrastructure builds

Preferred qualifications

- 3+ years of working directly with engineering teams experience

title: Environmental Ops Manager, re:Cycle Reverse Logistics
descriptionHtml:
re:Cycle Reverse Logistics is an electronics processing, reuse, and recycling company that extends the life of used electronic equipment through reuse, repair, and recycling. We are a stand-alone company within the Amazon corporate family that provides services to other Amazon companies, specializing in the handling of electronic equipment originally used in data centers.

We are looking for an Environmental Operations Manager to support our Reverse Logistics operation. Our mission is to manage and scale information technology asset disposition (ITAD) services for used electronics and electronic equipment (UEEE) through secure and environmentally sustainable practices supporting asset recovery, reuse, recycling, and other circular economy initiatives.

The Environmental Operations Manager will report to the re:Cycle Reverse Logistics Global EHS Manager and support environmental compliance across RRL operations. This role covers a range of environmental compliance programs including waste management, stormwater management, air quality compliance, spill prevention, and environmental permitting.


Key job responsibilities
• Support environmental compliance programs for re:Cycle Reverse Logistics by helping ensure operations meet applicable regulations and standards.
• Assist with compliance activities related to local, state, and federal environmental regulations, permit conditions, and Amazon policy for facilities managing end-of-life electronic equipment.
• Support stormwater compliance programs, including SWPPP maintenance, routine inspections, and sampling activities.
• Assist with air quality compliance activities, including emissions tracking, permit compliance, and regulatory reporting.
• Help develop and maintain SPCC plans and support spill prevention and countermeasure requirements.
• Support ISO 14001 and R2 certification programs by helping maintain audit-ready conditions at assigned facilities.
• Contribute to the development and maintenance of environmental standard operating procedures (SOPs), including waste handling and documentation procedures.
• Support the proper handling, tracking, and disposition of Focus Materials (e.g., PCBs, mercury-containing devices, batteries, circuit boards) in accordance with applicable regulations.
• Collaborate with operations teams, the RRL Commercial Team, and other stakeholders to support audit findings and corrective actions.
• Participate in environmental compliance audits and assist with follow-up activities.
• Support the waste vendor vetting process, including vendor qualification reviews and compliance monitoring.
• Coordinate with the RRL HSSE team to help identify and mitigate environmental risks within work processes.
• Assist with the preparation and submission of regulatory reports and permit-related documentation.
• Conduct environmental incident investigations and help develop corrective actions under guidance from senior team members.
• Use data and environmental best practices to support informed business decisions.


About the team

- Bachelor's degree in Environmental Science, Environmental Engineering, Chemistry, Chemical Engineering, or related field
